models.name: ecommerce_mall_categories
models.description: Product category taxonomy and hierarchical structure for organizing products. Categories provide the foundational organization system that sellers use to classify products and customers use for browsing and navigation. The category system supports multi-level hierarchies where categories can have parent categories, enabling flexible organizational structures from broad top-level categories down to specific product types. Each category defines attributes that products in that category must or optionally provide, ensuring consistent product information at the database level.

foreignFields.name: parent_category_id
foreignFields.description: Optional parent category for hierarchical organization. Enables multi-level category structure where each category can have a parent category. Self-referencing relationship to ecommerce_mall_categories. Null for top-level categories.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name displayed to customers and sellers. Must be unique within the platform. Examples: Electronics, Clothing, Home & Garden.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: URL-friendly slug for the category used in category pages. Generated from category name, lowercase with hyphens. Example: home-and-garden.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the category explaining what products it contains. Displayed on category pages to help customers understand category scope.

plainFields.name: icon_url
plainFields.description: URL to icon or image representing the category. Displayed in category navigation and category pages for visual identification.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Sort order for displaying categories in navigation menus and category lists. Lower numbers appear first. Allows admins to customize category display order.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the category is visible to customers. Inactive categories are hidden from browsing but existing products remain in the system. Allows temporarily disabling categories without data deletion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the category was created. Used for audit trail and category age tracking.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the category. Tracks when category information was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, category is considered deleted but data is retained for compliance and historical purposes. Used for soft deletion allowing data recovery.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_category_attributes
models.description: Attribute specifications for product categories. Each category can define required and optional attributes that products must provide (e.g., apparel requires size, color; electronics requires specifications, warranty). Category attributes establish consistency expectations for products in each category, enabling structured product information capture and display. Attributes defined here are enforced when sellers create products in these categories.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_category_id
foreignFields.description: The category this attribute belongs to. Links to ecommerce_mall_categories.id. Cannot be changed after creation.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Attribute name that sellers provide values for. Examples: Color, Size, Material, Warranty Period, Specifications.

plainFields.name: attribute_type
plainFields.description: Data type for the attribute value: text (free text input), select (predefined options), multiselect (multiple options), number, boolean. Determines how sellers input values for this attribute.

plainFields.name: is_required
plainFields.description: Whether sellers must provide a value for this attribute when creating products in this category. Required attributes must have values; optional attributes can be left empty.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display order for attributes in the product creation form. Lower numbers appear first, organizing the form for better user experience.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the attribute was defined. Used for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to the attribute definition.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_platform_settings
models.description: System-wide configuration settings that control platform behavior and policies. Platform settings define defaults for commissions, return windows, payment methods, notification preferences, feature flags, and other system-wide parameters. Admin users modify these settings to configure platform behavior without code changes. Settings are referenced by multiple systems (order processing, refund handling, payment processing) to enforce consistent policies across the platform.

plainFields.name: setting_key
plainFields.description: Unique identifier for the setting. Examples: default_commission_rate, return_window_days, payment_retry_attempts, platform_name, support_email. Used as lookup key when retrieving setting values.

plainFields.name: setting_value
plainFields.description: The configuration value for the setting. Stored as string and converted to appropriate type (number, boolean, etc.) by application code. Examples: 15, 30, 5, ecommercemall@company.com.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description explaining what this setting controls and how it affects platform behavior. Displayed in admin configuration UI to guide admins in setting values.

plainFields.name: setting_type
plainFields.description: Data type for the setting: string, integer, decimal, boolean, email, url. Indicates how the value should be interpreted and validated by the application.

plainFields.name: is_editable
plainFields.description: Whether admins can modify this setting through the admin panel. Core system settings may be read-only to prevent misconfiguration. Editable settings can be changed by authorized admins.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the setting was created. Used for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to the setting value. Tracks when configuration was last changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Allows settings to be archived without deletion. Deleted settings are not used but data is retained for compliance.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_regions
models.description: Geographic regions supported by the platform for shipping, tax, and currency operations. Regions represent distinct geographic areas (countries, states, provinces) where the platform operates and where specific shipping methods, tax rules, and currencies apply. Regions are referenced when calculating shipping costs, applying taxes, and displaying region-specific information. The platform uses regions to determine which shipping carriers serve an address and which tax rules apply.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Region name displayed in dropdowns and configuration. Examples: United States, California, United Kingdom, Japan. Unique within the platform.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Standardized code for the region. Uses ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 for countries (US, GB, JP) or ISO 3166-2 for states (US-CA, US-TX). Used for lookups and integrations.

plainFields.name: region_type
plainFields.description: Type of region: country or state/province. Indicates the hierarchical level. Used for organizing regions and determining shipping zone calculations.

plainFields.name: parent_region_code
plainFields.description: For states/provinces, the country code of the parent country. Enables hierarchical organization (e.g., CA region's parent is US). For countries, null.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the region is available for operations (shipping, tax calculations). Inactive regions are not presented to customers as shipping destinations or tax jurisdictions.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the region was added to the system. Used for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to region configuration.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_currencies
models.description: Currencies supported by the platform for pricing and payment processing. Each currency represents a specific monetary unit (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, etc.) that the platform uses for displaying prices, calculating totals, and processing payments. Currencies are associated with regions (USD for US, EUR for EU countries, GBP for UK) to determine which currencies customers see when shopping. The platform uses currency records to format prices correctly and convert between currencies for international orders.

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: ISO 4217 currency code (3 characters). Examples: USD (US Dollar), EUR (Euro), GBP (British Pound), JPY (Japanese Yen). Unique identifier for the currency.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Full currency name for display in user interfaces. Examples: US Dollar, Euro, British Pound, Japanese Yen.

plainFields.name: symbol
plainFields.description: Currency symbol for displaying prices. Examples: $ for USD, € for EUR, £ for GBP, ¥ for JPY. Used in price formatting for customer display.

plainFields.name: decimal_places
plainFields.description: Number of decimal places for this currency. Most currencies use 2 (USD, EUR = $19.99), some use 0 (JPY = ¥1999), some use 3 (KWD = د.ك 19.999). Used for price rounding and formatting.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether the currency is currently available for transactions and display. Inactive currencies are not presented to customers but existing prices in that currency are preserved for historical records.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the currency was added to the platform. Used for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to currency configuration.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_tax_rules
models.description: Tax calculation rules that apply to orders based on shipping destination and product category. Tax rules define the percentage of tax to apply and the conditions under which they apply (which region, which product category, base amount calculation). The platform uses tax rules to automatically calculate tax amounts during checkout based on the customer's shipping address and the products they're purchasing. Tax rules can be region-specific (different tax rates for different countries/states) and may vary by product category.

plainFields.name: region_code
plainFields.description: Region code (e.g., US, US-CA, GB) that this tax rule applies to. The tax rate specified applies when the customer's shipping address is in this region. Must match a region code in ecommerce_mall_regions table.

plainFields.name: category_name
plainFields.description: Product category this tax rule applies to. If null, the rule applies to all categories (default tax rate). If specified, applies only to products in that category. Enables category-specific tax rates (e.g., groceries may be tax-exempt).

plainFields.name: tax_percentage
plainFields.description: The tax rate as a percentage (0-100). Examples: 8.5 for 8.5%, 0 for tax-exempt, 20 for 20% VAT. Stored as decimal for accurate calculations.

plainFields.name: tax_basis
plainFields.description: What the tax percentage applies to: subtotal (merchandise only), subtotal_with_shipping (includes shipping cost), or gross (after discounts). Determines how tax is calculated for orders in this jurisdiction.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this tax rule is currently applied during tax calculations. Inactive rules are not used but are retained for historical reference and potential reactivation.

plainFields.name: effective_from
plainFields.description: Date when this tax rule becomes effective. Used for tracking tax law changes. Orders after this date use this rule; orders before may use older rules.

plainFields.name: effective_until
plainFields.description: Date when this tax rule expires. When set, the rule is no longer used after this date. Used for temporary tax changes or seasonal variations. Null means rule has no end date.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the tax rule was created. Used for audit trail.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last update to the tax rule.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_customers
models.description:
Registered customer accounts for the e-commerce platform. Customers are authenticated users who can browse products, manage shopping carts, place orders, and interact with the marketplace through reviews and wishlists.

Each customer account is created through self-registration with email verification. The account stores authentication credentials (hashed password), profile information, and account status tracking. Customer accounts are linked to multiple addresses, payment methods, orders, and sessions for multi-device support.

Soft deletion is supported to maintain audit trails while allowing account recovery. Account status transitions from pending_verification → active → suspended/deactivated as needed.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Customer's email address used for authentication and communication. Must be unique across all customers. Email verification required before account activation.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password using bcrypt (work factor 12). Never stores plain text passwords. Used for login authentication and password reset functionality.

plainFields.name: first_name
plainFields.description: Customer's first name. Minimum 2 characters, maximum 50 characters. Used for personalization and order communication.

plainFields.name: last_name
plainFields.description: Customer's last name. Minimum 2 characters, maximum 50 characters. Used for personalization and order communication.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Customer's phone number for order coordination and customer support. Optional field, customer can add/update during account setup or checkout.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the customer's email address has been verified. Customers must verify email before placing orders. Set to true only after clicking verification link.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current account status. Valid values: pending_verification (awaiting email verification), active (verified and able to purchase), suspended (temporarily disabled by admin), deactivated (voluntarily paused by customer). Defaults to pending_verification.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of account creation. Set when customer completes initial registration form.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last account modification. Updated whenever customer profile, password, or settings are changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Set when customer requests account deletion. NULL means account is active. Allows account recovery and maintains audit trail.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for customer users. Each session represents a login instance on a specific device/browser. Sessions store connection context (IP, URL, referrer) and track session lifecycle from creation to expiration.

Customers can maintain multiple concurrent sessions across different devices. Each session is identified by a unique ID and tracks the authenticated customer. Sessions expire after extended inactivity, forcing re-authentication. Session creation automatically occurs on successful login. Session expiration can be triggered by logout, browser close, or inactivity timeout.

Session data is used for security monitoring (detect unusual access patterns), audit logging (track user actions per session), and device management (customers can view and revoke sessions from specific devices).

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the authenticated customer. Each session belongs to exactly one customer. Relationship is many-to-one (customer can have multiple sessions). {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device/network creating this session. Used for security monitoring (detect suspicious geographic changes, multiple simultaneous logins from different IPs).

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL/href where the session was created. Captures the entry point to the application (homepage, product page, checkout, etc.).

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer URL indicating how customer arrived at the platform (direct, search engine, social media, email link, etc.). Used for marketing attribution and traffic analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp (when customer logged in). UTC timezone. Used for session age tracking and SLA monitoring.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp (when customer logged out or session was terminated). NULL means session is still active. Set to current timestamp when session expires due to inactivity or explicit logout.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_sellers
models.description:
Registered seller/merchant accounts on the marketplace. Sellers are independent business entities that create stores, manage product catalogs, process orders, and track sales performance.

Each seller account is created through business registration requiring business information (name, registration number), contact details, and banking information for commission settlements. Sellers must complete verification (typically 5 business days) before they can list products.

Seller accounts track account status (pending_verification, active, suspended, deactivated, rejected) and support soft deletion. Sellers have their own authentication sessions, separate store profiles, and linked payment settlement records. Seller ratings are calculated from customer feedback across all their orders.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Seller's business email address used for authentication and official communication. Must be unique across all sellers. Email verification required during registration process.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password using bcrypt (work factor 12). Used for seller dashboard login. Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: business_name
plainFields.description: Official business name for the seller. Used for store branding and legal identification. Displayed prominently on seller's storefront.

plainFields.name: business_registration_number
plainFields.description: Business registration or tax identification number from business registration authority. Verified during seller application. Used for legal compliance and commission calculations.

plainFields.name: business_email
plainFields.description: Official business email address (may differ from login email). Used for formal communications, notifications, and official documents.

plainFields.name: business_phone
plainFields.description: Business phone number for platform communication and order coordination. Required for contacting seller regarding account, operations, or disputes.

plainFields.name: business_address
plainFields.description: Physical business address (street, city, postal code, country). Used for verification, compliance, and legal identification.

plainFields.name: bank_account_holder_name
plainFields.description: Name on bank account for commission payments. Must match bank records exactly for settlement transfers to succeed.

plainFields.name: bank_name
plainFields.description: Name of the bank where seller's account is held. Used for identifying bank for international transfers and verification.

plainFields.name: bank_routing_number
plainFields.description: Routing number for bank transfers (US format) or equivalent for other countries. Required for direct deposit settlement payments.

plainFields.name: bank_account_number
plainFields.description: Bank account number for receiving commission payments. Encrypted before storage. Used for automated settlement transfers.

plainFields.name: tax_id
plainFields.description: Tax identification number for the seller's jurisdiction. Used for compliance, tax reporting, and 1099 form generation.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current seller account status. Valid values: pending_verification (awaiting business verification), active (verified and can list products), suspended (temporarily disabled by admin, no new listings or orders), deactivated (voluntarily paused by seller), rejected (application rejected). Defaults to pending_verification.

plainFields.name: email_verified
plainFields.description: Whether the seller's email has been verified. Required before seller can list products. Set to true after email verification link is clicked.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller application was submitted. Marks the start of verification process.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last account modification (status changes, banking info updates, profile changes).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Set when seller requests account closure. NULL means account is active. Allows account recovery and maintains order/transaction history.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for seller users. Each session represents a login instance from a seller on a specific device/browser. Sessions store connection context (IP address, URL, referrer) and track session state.

Sellers can maintain multiple concurrent sessions across different devices and browsers. Each session tracks the authenticated seller and records connection metadata for security monitoring and audit purposes.

Session data enables: security monitoring (detect unusual access patterns from unexpected locations), device management (sellers can view active sessions and revoke access from specific devices), and audit logging (track seller actions per session for compliance).

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the authenticated seller. Each session belongs to exactly one seller. Relationship is many-to-one (seller can have multiple concurrent sessions). {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device/network initiating this session. Used for security monitoring (detect logins from unusual locations or multiple concurrent locations).

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL/href where the session was created. Captures the entry point (dashboard, product management, orders, analytics, etc.).

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer URL showing how seller arrived at the platform (direct access, email link, bookmark, etc.).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp (when seller logged in). UTC timezone. Used for session age tracking and SLA monitoring.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp (when seller logged out or session was terminated). NULL means session is still active. Set to current timestamp when session expires.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admins
models.description:
System administrator accounts with elevated permissions for platform oversight and management. Admins have full access to user management, order management, product oversight, dispute resolution, analytics, and system configuration.

Unlike customer and seller accounts which are created through public registration, admin accounts are created internally by system owners or existing admins. Admin accounts require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for enhanced security due to elevated privileges.

Admin authentication uses separate admin-only sessions. Admins cannot simultaneously operate as customers or sellers (separate account types). All admin actions are fully logged in audit trails for compliance and security purposes.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description: Admin's email address used for authentication and official communication. Must be unique across all admins. Verified during admin account creation.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description: Hashed password using bcrypt (work factor 12). Admin passwords must meet high complexity requirements (minimum 16 characters with mixed case, numbers, special characters). Never stored in plain text.

plainFields.name: full_name
plainFields.description: Admin's full name. Used for admin action logging and audit trails to identify who performed each action.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description: Admin role designation. Valid values: super_admin (full platform access), operations_admin (order/customer management), product_admin (product catalog oversight), seller_admin (seller account management), analytics_admin (reporting only). Defines permission scope.

plainFields.name: mfa_enabled
plainFields.description: Whether multi-factor authentication is enabled for this admin account. Required for all admin accounts. Admin must provide MFA code (TOTP) in addition to password during login.

plainFields.name: mfa_secret
plainFields.description: Encrypted TOTP secret for multi-factor authentication. Used to generate time-based one-time passwords for login. Encrypted before storage for security.

plainFields.name: account_status
plainFields.description: Current account status. Valid values: active (can login), deactivated (disabled by system owner). Admins cannot suspend their own accounts (prevents accidental lockout).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when admin account was created. Set by system owner or existing admin during account creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last account modification (password changes, role changes, MFA updates).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Set when admin account is deactivated. NULL means account is active. Allows account recovery.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_sessions
models.description:
Authentication sessions for admin users. Each session represents an authenticated admin login on a specific device/browser. Sessions store connection context (IP, URL, referrer) and track session lifecycle.

Admin sessions are monitored more strictly than regular user sessions for security. Unusual access patterns (logins from unexpected locations, multiple simultaneous logins from different countries, unusual times) trigger security alerts and may require additional verification.

Each admin session is tied to a specific admin user and records connection metadata for comprehensive audit logging of all admin activities on the platform.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the authenticated admin. Each session belongs to exactly one admin. Relationship is many-to-one (admin can have multiple concurrent sessions). {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description: IP address of the device/network accessing the admin panel. Used for security monitoring (detect unusual geographic locations, rate limiting, suspicious access patterns).

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description: URL/href where the admin panel session was initiated. Captures entry point to admin system.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description: HTTP referrer URL showing how admin accessed the platform (direct link, bookmark, email notification, etc.).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Session creation timestamp (when admin logged into admin panel). UTC timezone. Used for session age tracking and security monitoring.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description: Session expiration timestamp (when admin logged out or session was terminated). NULL means session is still active. Admin sessions have shorter timeout (30 minutes) than customer sessions.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_addresses
models.description:
Delivery addresses associated with customer accounts. Customers can save multiple addresses and select one during checkout for order delivery.

Each address is linked to a specific customer and includes complete delivery information (street, city, postal code, country) plus contact details (phone number). Addresses are not independently managed - they are managed through the customer's account address management interface.

One address can be marked as the customer's default address for faster checkout. Addresses cannot be deleted if currently associated with active orders (awaiting fulfillment or delivery). Soft deletion preserves address history after completion of all associated orders.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the customer who owns this address. Each address belongs to exactly one customer. Relationship is many-to-one (customer can have multiple addresses). {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: recipient_name
plainFields.description: Name of the person receiving the delivery at this address. Used on shipping labels and delivery instructions.

plainFields.name: street_address_line_1
plainFields.description: Primary street address (house number and street name). Required for all addresses.

plainFields.name: street_address_line_2
plainFields.description: Secondary street address information (apartment number, suite, building name, etc.). Optional for addresses that don't have additional location information.

plainFields.name: city
plainFields.description: City or municipality name where the address is located.

plainFields.name: state_or_province
plainFields.description: State, province, or region name. Used for tax calculation and shipping routing.

plainFields.name: postal_code
plainFields.description: Postal code or ZIP code. Format varies by country. Validated for correct format based on selected country.

plainFields.name: country
plainFields.description: Country name or country code. Determines tax rules, shipping options, and currency. Validates that seller ships to this country.

plainFields.name: phone_number
plainFields.description: Contact phone number for the delivery address. Used by shipping carrier for delivery coordination if needed (e.g., to confirm door access).

plainFields.name: is_default
plainFields.description: Whether this is the customer's default address for checkout. Only one address per customer can be marked as default. When customer places order, default address is pre-selected for speed.

plainFields.name: address_label
plainFields.description: Customer-defined label for this address (e.g., 'Home', 'Work', 'Parent's House'). Helps customer identify addresses quickly when managing multiple saved addresses.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when address was added to customer's account.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last address modification (correcting typo, updating apartment number, etc.).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Set when customer deletes address from their account. NULL means address is active. Allows recovery if customer needs address back.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_profiles
models.description:
Store profile information for sellers. Each seller has exactly one profile storing their storefront branding, description, and store-specific policies.

The seller profile contains the public-facing information displayed to customers visiting the seller's store page, including store name, description, logo/banner images, and contact information. Store policies (return policy, refund policy, shipping policy) are stored here and displayed to customers before purchase.

Profile information is managed by the seller through their dashboard and updated immediately (within 2 minutes) for customer visibility.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the seller who owns this profile. Each seller has exactly one profile. One-to-one relationship with ecommerce_mall_sellers. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: store_name
plainFields.description: Public display name for the seller's store. Used on storefront, in search results, and in product listings. Can differ from business legal name for branding purposes.

plainFields.name: store_description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the store, products, and seller's business. Displayed on store homepage. 500-2000 characters. Optional field allowing seller to tell their story.

plainFields.name: logo_image_url
plainFields.description: URL to store logo image (200x200px recommended, max 2MB). Displayed in store header and in product listings. Optional - store can operate without logo.

plainFields.name: banner_image_url
plainFields.description: URL to store banner/header image (1200x300px recommended, max 5MB). Displayed at top of store page for branding. Optional field.

plainFields.name: contact_phone
plainFields.description: Public phone number for customers to contact the seller. Optional - seller may prefer email/messaging only.

plainFields.name: contact_email
plainFields.description: Public email address for customer inquiries. Can differ from business email for customer-facing communications.

plainFields.name: return_policy
plainFields.description: Seller's return and refund policy displayed to customers. Specifies return window (days), restocking fees if any, condition requirements, and exclusions. 500-2000 characters.

plainFields.name: shipping_policy
plainFields.description: Seller's shipping policy including processing time, available shipping methods, and any regional restrictions. Displayed during checkout. 500-2000 characters.

plainFields.name: business_hours
plainFields.description: Seller's operating hours (e.g., 'Mon-Fri 9am-5pm EST'). Displayed on store page and helps set customer expectations for response times.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller profile was created (typically when seller account was created).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of last profile update (when seller edited store information).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_methods
models.description:
Saved payment methods (credit cards, debit cards, digital wallets) for customer accounts. Customers can save multiple payment methods and select one during checkout for transaction processing.

Payment method information is tokenized - the system never stores full credit card numbers, CVV codes, or complete payment card data. Instead, tokenized references are stored for compliance with PCI DSS requirements. Customers can manage their saved payment methods, set a default method for faster checkout, and delete methods they no longer use.

Payment methods are primary entities requiring independent CRUD operations since customers directly manage them from their account settings.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Foreign key referencing the customer who owns this payment method. Each payment method belongs to exactly one customer. Relationship is many-to-one (customer can have multiple payment methods). {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: payment_type
plainFields.description: Type of payment method. Valid values: credit_card, debit_card, digital_wallet (Apple Pay, Google Pay), bank_transfer. Determines how payment is processed and displayed to customer.

plainFields.name: payment_token
plainFields.description: Tokenized reference to the actual payment method from payment processor. This is a unique, non-reversible token representing the saved payment method. Never exposes actual card/account numbers.

plainFields.name: card_last_four
plainFields.description: Last four digits of credit/debit card number (e.g., '4242'). Displayed to customer for identification. Only these digits are stored; full card number is never stored.

plainFields.name: card_brand
plainFields.description: Brand/issuer of the card. Valid values: visa, mastercard, amex, discover, diners. Displayed in payment method list. NULL for non-card payment types.

plainFields.name: expiration_month
plainFields.description: Card expiration month (1-12). Used for determining if card is expired. NULL for non-card payment types.

plainFields.name: expiration_year

plainFields.name: cardholder_name

plainFields.name: billing_address

models.name: ecommerce_mall_products
models.description:
Core product catalog entities representing logical product groupings.

Products serve as the parent entity for all product variants and contain general product information shared across all configurations. Each product is owned and managed by exactly one seller and belongs to one or more product categories. Products maintain complete lifecycle management through status tracking (draft, published, unpublished, archived) enabling sellers to control visibility and availability.

The product entity stores product-level information that applies uniformly across all variants, including descriptions, manufacturer details, and general specifications. Product-specific images and attributes are linked through separate related tables, enabling granular media and specification management.

Soft deletion is supported through the deleted_at timestamp, preserving product history for compliance and analytics while removing products from active visibility. Products are indexed by seller for efficient dashboard operations and by category for catalog organization.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller who owns and manages this product. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: code
plainFields.description: Seller-defined product SKU code for inventory reference. Unique per seller within category.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Product name displayed to customers. 100-255 characters, unique per seller per category.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed product description with formatting support (500-5000 characters). Includes features, benefits, care instructions, and specifications.

plainFields.name: brand
plainFields.description: Product brand or manufacturer name for categorization and filtering.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Product lifecycle status: draft (unpublished), published (visible), unpublished (hidden temporarily), archived (retired). Controls customer visibility and purchase availability.

plainFields.name: condition
plainFields.description: Product condition: New, Like New, Refurbished, Used. Indicates product quality and origin.

plainFields.name: weight
plainFields.description: Product weight in kilograms for shipping calculations. Required for accurate rate quotes.

plainFields.name: length
plainFields.description: Product length in centimeters for shipping and packaging dimensions.

plainFields.name: width
plainFields.description: Product width in centimeters for shipping and packaging dimensions.

plainFields.name: height
plainFields.description: Product height in centimeters for shipping and packaging dimensions.

plainFields.name: material
plainFields.description: Primary material composition (textile, plastic, metal, wood, etc.). Used for filtering and category-specific requirements.

plainFields.name: care_instructions
plainFields.description: Detailed care and maintenance instructions for the product. Helps customers properly use and maintain purchased items.

plainFields.name: warranty_months

plainFields.name: manufacturing_country

plainFields.name: is_configurable

plainFields.name: updated_at

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variants
models.description:
Specific product configurations defined by attribute combinations.

Variants represent distinct combinations of product attributes (such as color, size, material, or custom options) that constitute separate purchasable items. Each variant is uniquely identified by its attribute combination and linked to exactly one SKU for inventory tracking. Variants enable sellers to offer products in multiple configurations while maintaining a unified product identity.

Variants inherit product-level information (name, description, images) from their parent product but can have variant-specific pricing, images, and descriptions. This separation allows flexible product management where base information is shared but configuration-specific details can be customized.

Variants support the core e-commerce requirement of allowing customers to select product configurations during checkout. The variant structure enables precise inventory tracking at the SKU level while maintaining logical product grouping.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Parent product this variant belongs to. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: System-generated or seller-provided SKU code uniquely identifying this variant. Used for inventory tracking and order fulfillment.

plainFields.name: attribute_combination
plainFields.description: JSON string encoding the attribute combination defining this variant (e.g., {"color": "Red", "size": "Large"}). Used to identify and group variants by configuration.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Human-readable variant name shown to customers (e.g., "Red, Size Large"). Generated from attributes or manually set by seller.

plainFields.name: base_price
plainFields.description: Base price in the platform's default currency (USD or regional equivalent). Variant-specific pricing allows different costs for different configurations.

plainFields.name: cost_of_goods
plainFields.description: Seller's cost to source this variant (not visible to customers). Used for margin calculations and seller analytics.

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: URL to variant-specific product image. If empty, variant uses parent product images. Allows showing actual color/configuration to customers.

plainFields.name: description_override
plainFields.description: Variant-specific description override (e.g., "This version includes extra padding"). Supplements parent product description with configuration-specific details.

plainFields.name: is_available
plainFields.description: Whether this variant is currently available for purchase. Can be false while product is published (e.g., out of stock, discontinued specific configuration).

plainFields.name: sort_order
plainFields.description: Display order for variant in customer selection interface. Lower numbers display first.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when variant was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when variant was last modified.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_skus
models.description:
Stock-keeping units tracking inventory at the variant level.

SKUs represent the atomic unit for inventory management, linking each product variant to a unique inventory tracking identifier. Each SKU maintains a 1:1 relationship with a product variant, enabling precise stock tracking for specific configurations. SKUs serve as the authoritative record for inventory quantities, reservations, and historical stock data.

The SKU record stores inventory state information required for accurate stock management, including current available quantity, reserved inventory for pending orders, and low-stock thresholds. SKUs are referenced during order placement to verify availability and allocate inventory, ensuring accurate inventory counts and preventing overselling.

SKU records integrate with the inventory management system, linking to stock level records, reservations, and adjustment history. This separation of inventory tracking from variant definition enables efficient inventory operations without coupling product configuration management to stock management.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Product variant this SKU represents. 1:1 relationship with variant. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: sku_code
plainFields.description: Unique SKU identifier matching variant's sku_code. Redundant copy for inventory system efficiency and denormalization.

plainFields.name: total_stock
plainFields.description: Total physical inventory quantity available. Sum of available plus reserved plus damaged units.

plainFields.name: reserved_stock
plainFields.description: Inventory quantity allocated to confirmed but unfulfilled orders. Calculated as sum of inventory reservations for pending orders.

plainFields.name: available_stock
plainFields.description: Calculated available quantity for purchase (total_stock - reserved_stock - damaged). Used for checkout validation and display.

plainFields.name: damaged_stock
plainFields.description: Inventory quantity determined to be defective or unsaleable. Tracked separately for inventory accuracy and loss analysis.

plainFields.name: low_stock_threshold
plainFields.description: Seller-configured quantity threshold triggering low-stock alerts. Defaults based on product price tier. When available_stock <= threshold, alerts are sent.

plainFields.name: reorder_point
plainFields.description: Calculated quantity suggesting when seller should reorder based on sales velocity. Future feature for demand planning.

plainFields.name: last_stock_audit_date
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent physical inventory count verification. Used to assess inventory accuracy and identify discrepancies.

plainFields.name: last_audit_result
plainFields.description: Result of last inventory audit: Pass (matched), Fail (discrepancy), or Pending (not yet audited).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when SKU record was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when SKU inventory quantities were last modified.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_options
models.description:
Configurable product attributes enabling variant definition.

Product options represent the attributes that can be selected when configuring product variants (such as color, size, material, or custom options). Each option defines a set of possible values that customers can choose from when purchasing. Options are product-level configuration templates that define what attributes are available for selection.

Options are typically drawn from a standard set (Color, Size, Material) but sellers can also define custom options for specialized products. Each option has a name, description, and a set of associated option values representing the specific choices available for that option.

The product options table serves as a configuration registry, defining what variant attributes are configurable for each product. This separation enables efficient management of variant possibilities without requiring variant records to store attribute metadata, supporting scalable product variant management.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product this option applies to. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Option name (e.g., "Color", "Size", "Material"). Standard values include Color, Size, Style, Capacity, Width, Length. Supports custom options for specialized products.

plainFields.name: display_name
plainFields.description: Customer-facing option label (e.g., "Available Colors", "Size Options"). Used in variant selection interface.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Description of what this option represents and how customer selection affects the product. Helps customers understand option impact.

plainFields.name: is_required
plainFields.description: Whether customer must select this option to complete product configuration (true) or if it's optional (false). Controls variant selection requirements.

plainFields.name: input_type
plainFields.description: How option values are presented to customers: dropdown (select from list), color_swatch (visual color selection), size_chart (size selection), text_input (customer enters custom value), numeric (numeric input with range).

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Order in which options appear in variant selection interface. Lower numbers display first.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when option was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when option was last modified.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_option_values
models.description:
Specific values available for product options.

Option values represent the distinct choices available for each product option. For example, a Color option might have values like Red, Blue, Green, etc., while a Size option might have S, M, L, XL. Option values are the concrete selections customers make when configuring product variants.

Each option value stores its display information, including the value name, color code (for color options), and sort order. Option values can be standard predefined values (from platform color palette or size charts) or custom values defined by the seller for specialty items.

Option values are linked to product options, creating the complete option configuration template. When sellers define variant attributes, they specify which option values are available for each option, and the system automatically generates all possible variant combinations from the selected option values.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_option_id
foreignFields.description: Product option this value belongs to. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_options.id}

plainFields.name: value_name
plainFields.description: Display name of this option value (e.g., "Red", "Large", "Cotton"). Shown to customers during variant selection.

plainFields.name: value_code
plainFields.description: Internal code for the value (e.g., "red", "lg", "cotton"). Used in attribute_combination JSON and system processing.

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description: Hex color code for color-type options (e.g., "#FF0000" for red). Used for visual color swatches in UI.

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: Image URL showing this option value (e.g., shoe in this color). Used for visual representation in variant selection.

plainFields.name: additional_cost
plainFields.description: Additional price for this option value (e.g., larger sizes might cost more). Allows price variation based on selected options.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display order of this value within the option. Lower numbers display first.

plainFields.name: is_available
plainFields.description: Whether this option value is currently available for new variant creation. Can be false for discontinued options.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when option value was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when option value was last modified.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_images
models.description:
Product and variant-specific images for customer viewing.

Product images represent the visual media assets associated with products and variants, enabling customers to see what they're purchasing. Images can be attached at the product level (applying to all variants) or at the variant level (showing specific configurations like a product in a particular color).

Each image record stores the image URL, image type (main, detail, lifestyle, size_chart), display order, and variant-specific association. The system automatically generates optimized versions for different device sizes (mobile, tablet, desktop) and formats (WebP, PNG) to ensure fast loading and proper display across platforms.

Images are critical for e-commerce conversion, allowing customers to evaluate products visually before purchase. Variant-specific images showing the actual color or configuration help reduce returns and increase customer satisfaction by eliminating ambiguity about product appearance.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product these images belong to. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_variant_id
foreignFields.description: Specific variant this image applies to (if variant-specific). If null, image applies to all variants. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_variants.id}

plainFields.name: image_url
plainFields.description: URL to the product image hosted on CDN. Optimized for web delivery with format conversion and responsive sizing.

plainFields.name: image_type
plainFields.description: Image purpose/type: main (primary product view), detail (close-up of features), lifestyle (product in use), size_chart (size reference), comparison (comparison to similar items), other.

plainFields.name: alt_text
plainFields.description: Accessibility alt text describing image content. Used for SEO and screen readers. Example: "Blue Nike Running Shoe, lateral view showing cushioning detail".

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display order of image in product gallery. Lower numbers show first. Main image typically has order 1.

plainFields.name: is_primary
plainFields.description: Whether this is the primary/featured image shown in search results and product thumbnails. Only one per product should be primary.

plainFields.name: file_size_kb
plainFields.description: Original uploaded image file size in kilobytes. Helps track optimization effectiveness and storage usage.

plainFields.name: image_width
plainFields.description: Original image width in pixels. Used for responsive sizing and aspect ratio calculations.

plainFields.name: image_height
plainFields.description: Original image height in pixels. Used for responsive sizing and aspect ratio calculations.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when image was uploaded.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when image metadata was last updated (alt text, order, etc.).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_attributes
models.description:
Product specifications and detailed attribute information.

Product attributes represent detailed product characteristics and specifications beyond variant-defining options. Attributes provide structured, searchable information about product properties such as material composition, care instructions, safety certifications, and technical specifications.

Unlike options which define variant configurations, attributes are fixed product specifications that apply uniformly across all variants (or can vary by variant if needed). Attributes enable rich product information presentation and support category-specific attribute requirements, allowing customers to compare products based on detailed specifications.

Attributes are commonly used for filtering and search refinement, helping customers find products matching their specific needs (e.g., filter shirts by material = cotton). The attribute structure supports both predefined category-specific attributes and custom seller-defined attributes for specialized product types.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product this attribute describes. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

plainFields.name: attribute_name
plainFields.description: Name of the attribute (e.g., "Material", "Care Instructions", "Water Resistance", "Warranty"). Maps to category-defined attribute templates.

plainFields.name: attribute_value
plainFields.description: Specific value for this attribute (e.g., "Cotton", "Machine wash cold", "IP67 waterproof"). Can be predefined or free-form text depending on attribute type.

plainFields.name: value_type
plainFields.description: Data type of the attribute value: text (free text), predefined (from standard list), numeric (number with unit), boolean (yes/no), list (comma-separated values).

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Display order of attribute in product detail page. Lower numbers display first.

plainFields.name: is_searchable
plainFields.description: Whether customers can filter products by this attribute in search/browse. Used to optimize search facets.

plainFields.name: is_comparable
plainFields.description: Whether this attribute should appear in product comparison tools. Helps customers compare similar products side-by-side.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when attribute was assigned to product.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when attribute value was last modified.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_stock_levels
models.description:
Real-time inventory tracking at the individual SKU level. This table maintains the authoritative source of truth for product variant stock quantities, preventing overselling and providing immediate visibility to customers and sellers.

Each SKU (Stock-Keeping Unit) represents a unique product variant combination (base product + color + size + options). This table tracks the current state: total available inventory, quantities reserved for pending orders, and stock status classification.

The system guarantees inventory accuracy through atomic transactions and prevents double-booking of inventory to multiple customers. Stock levels are updated in real-time when orders are placed, cancelled, or fulfilled, and when sellers manually adjust inventory.

Integration with order management ensures inventory reservations are created at checkout and confirmed at payment. Integration with product catalog displays current availability to customers. Sellers access this table through their inventory management dashboard.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the specific product variant's {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}. Each SKU has independent inventory tracking.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the seller who owns this product and manages this inventory. Enforces complete inventory isolation between sellers. Seller ID is inherited from the product_skus relationship's parent product.

plainFields.name: total_stock
plainFields.description: Total physical inventory quantity currently held. This is the complete count of all units available. Must be non-negative. Updated when orders are placed (decrease), cancelled (increase), or seller adjusts inventory.

plainFields.name: reserved_stock
plainFields.description: Quantity allocated to orders that are confirmed or processing but not yet shipped. Reserved inventory is unavailable for new customer purchases. Released back to available when orders are cancelled. Becomes sold inventory when orders are fulfilled and shipped.

plainFields.name: stock_status
plainFields.description: Current classification of this SKU's inventory status. Valid values: 'In Stock' (above low stock threshold), 'Low Stock' (at or below threshold but above zero), 'Out of Stock' (zero units available), 'Discontinued' (seller no longer offering this variant). Status determines customer visibility and add-to-cart availability.

plainFields.name: low_stock_threshold
plainFields.description: Seller-configured quantity that triggers low stock alerts. When available inventory equals or falls below this threshold, the system generates low stock alert notifications. Default thresholds: 5 for products <$50, 3 for products $50-$500, 1 for products >$500.

plainFields.name: last_updated_timestamp
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent inventory change. Updated whenever total_stock, reserved_stock, or stock_status changes. Provides audit trail of inventory modifications. Precision to the second.

plainFields.name: inventory_version
plainFields.description: Version number incremented with each inventory change. Prevents stale update conflicts in high-concurrency scenarios where multiple processes attempt simultaneous inventory modifications. Enables optimistic locking for data consistency.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this stock level record was initially created (typically when seller creates the product variant). Used for audit trail and historical reference.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent update to any field in this record. Updated whenever any inventory change occurs including stock quantity changes, status changes, or threshold adjustments.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_stock_reservations
models.description:
Temporary inventory holds during the checkout and order placement process. This table manages the inventory lifecycle from cart through order confirmation, preventing overselling when multiple customers purchase the same limited-stock item simultaneously.

Reservations are created when customers initiate checkout (soft reservation for 30 minutes), validated at payment time, and converted to permanent allocations when orders are confirmed. Reservations are released if checkout is abandoned, payment fails, or order is cancelled.

The system uses reservations to enable the customer experience of protecting their cart items through the checkout process while still making inventory available if customers abandon their carts. Automatic expiration of aged reservations returns inventory to available stock.

Reservations are strictly managed by the system and not directly visible to end users. They enable the atomic all-or-nothing order creation: either the entire order reserves inventory and is created, or nothing is reserved and order creation fails with specific error message.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the specific product variant being reserved. References {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}. Each SKU can have multiple reservations from different customers or carts.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the order that this inventory reservation belongs to. References {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}. When order is confirmed, reservation is converted to permanent allocation. When order is cancelled, reservation is released.

foreignFields.name: cart_session_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the shopping cart session. References {@link ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id}. During checkout, inventory is soft-reserved for the cart. If checkout completes, order_id is set and cart_session_id is cleared. If checkout abandoned, reservation expires.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the seller who owns this inventory. References {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. Enables seller-specific reservation tracking and isolation of inventory across sellers.

plainFields.name: reserved_quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units of this SKU that are being held by this reservation. Must be positive integer. Exactly matches the quantity the customer is attempting to purchase (no partial reservations allowed).

plainFields.name: reservation_type
plainFields.description: Classification of reservation lifecycle stage. Valid values: 'soft_reservation' (temporary hold during checkout, expires after 30 minutes), 'hard_reservation' (confirmed for confirmed orders, released when order shipped), 'expired' (aged soft reservation, inventory released back to available).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this reservation was created. For soft reservations, this is when customer initiated checkout. For hard reservations, this is when order was confirmed and payment succeeded.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when soft reservation automatically expires and inventory is released. Calculated as created_at + 30 minutes for soft reservations. NULL for hard reservations (no expiration).

plainFields.name: confirmed_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when soft reservation was confirmed/converted to hard reservation (order payment succeeded). NULL for soft reservations that haven't yet been confirmed.

plainFields.name: released_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this reservation was released/cancelled. Set when order is cancelled, checkout abandoned, or soft reservation expires. NULL for active reservations.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_stock_adjustments
models.description:
Record of inventory adjustments made by sellers and system processes. This table tracks all modifications to inventory quantities beyond normal order-based changes, providing complete audit trail for inventory reconciliation and compliance.

Adjustments capture manual seller corrections (damaged goods discovered, inventory count discrepancies), automatic system adjustments (order cancellations restoring stock, returns processed), and administrative corrections. Each adjustment includes detailed reason codes and optional notes for investigation.

Small adjustments (0-5 units) are applied immediately. Medium adjustments (5-25 units) require admin approval within 24 hours. Large adjustments (25+ units) require priority admin review within 4 hours. The approval workflow prevents fraud and ensures data integrity.

All adjustments are immutable once recorded (cannot be edited), maintaining strict audit trail. Adjustment history is available for 3+ years for compliance and forensic analysis.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the specific product variant being adjusted. References {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}. Each adjustment applies to one SKU only (no bulk adjustments in single record).

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the seller who requested or initiated this adjustment. References {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. Records which seller's inventory is being adjusted (audit trail).

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Link to related order if adjustment is order-related (cancellation, return, fulfillment). References {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}. NULL for non-order adjustments (damage, count correction, loss). Enables tracing adjustments back to specific orders.

foreignFields.name: admin_approver_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the admin user who approved this adjustment (if approval was required). References {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}. NULL for adjustments that didn't require approval (small amounts, automatic system adjustments) or those pending approval.

plainFields.name: original_quantity
plainFields.description: Inventory quantity before this adjustment was applied. Captured for audit trail and to enable reversal if needed. Used to calculate the adjustment delta (original - new = change amount).

plainFields.name: adjusted_quantity
plainFields.description: Inventory quantity after this adjustment is applied. New quantity that replaces the original quantity. Must be non-negative (system prevents negative inventory).

plainFields.name: adjustment_amount
plainFields.description: Calculated delta of the adjustment (adjusted_quantity - original_quantity). Positive for inventory increases, negative for decreases. Used for analytics and trend analysis (which adjustments reduce inventory most frequently).

plainFields.name: adjustment_reason
plainFields.description: Reason code for this adjustment from predefined list. Valid values: 'damage_discovered', 'inventory_count_correction', 'loss_or_theft', 'order_cancellation_restore', 'order_fulfillment_complete', 'return_item_received', 'restock_received', 'system_correction', 'supplier_error_correction', 'other'. Enables tracking patterns (which reasons cause most adjustments).

plainFields.name: detailed_notes
plainFields.description: Optional detailed explanation of the adjustment. Up to 1000 characters. Used for context beyond the reason code (e.g., 'Physical count was 15, system showed 10. Count performed by: John Smith on 2024-01-15'). Helps with investigation and prevents future discrepancies.

plainFields.name: approval_status
plainFields.description: Status of the adjustment in the approval workflow. Valid values: 'applied' (no approval required, already in effect), 'pending_approval' (waiting for admin review), 'approved' (admin approved, now applied), 'denied' (admin rejected, not applied), 'cancelled' (was pending or approved, now cancelled).

plainFields.name: approval_reason
plainFields.description: If approval_status is 'denied' or 'cancelled', this explains why. Helps seller understand rejection and prevents resubmission of same adjustment.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this adjustment request was submitted. For seller-initiated adjustments, this is when seller requested the adjustment. For system-initiated adjustments, this is when system created the adjustment.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this adjustment was approved by admin (if approval was required). NULL if adjustment didn't require approval or is still pending approval.

plainFields.name: applied_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this adjustment was actually applied to the stock_levels table. For small adjustments, same as created_at. For approved adjustments, same as approved_at. For denied adjustments, NULL (never applied).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_stock_history
models.description:
Complete immutable audit trail of all inventory movements and changes. This append-only table records every inventory adjustment with full context, enabling reconciliation, forensic analysis, and compliance reporting.

Unlike stock_levels which stores only current state, stock_history preserves all historical inventory states. Each entry represents a single inventory event: order placed (reduction), order cancelled (restoration), order fulfilled (permanent decrease), seller adjustment (manual change), return processed (increase), etc.

The historical record enables reconstruction of inventory state at any point in time (point-in-time recovery), investigation of discrepancies, trend analysis of inventory movements, and audit trail compliance. Entries are never deleted or modified (immutable log).

Daily reconciliation compares current recorded inventory against historical events to detect data corruption or unauthorized modifications. Historical data retained for 7+ years per compliance requirements.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the product variant whose inventory changed. References {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}. Each history entry tracks changes for one SKU.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the seller who owns this inventory. References {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. Enables seller-specific history queries and inventory isolation verification.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: Link to related order if inventory change is order-related (placed, cancelled, fulfilled, return). References {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}. NULL for non-order changes (manual adjustments, damage).

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Classification of the inventory event that triggered this history entry. Valid values: 'order_placed' (inventory reserved), 'order_cancelled' (inventory released), 'order_fulfilled' (inventory marked sold), 'manual_adjustment' (seller or admin adjusted), 'damage_recorded' (items found damaged), 'return_received' (customer returned items), 'return_rejected' (return not accepted), 'inventory_count_correction' (count discrepancy fixed), 'system_correction' (system error corrected), 'restock' (new inventory received).

plainFields.name: quantity_before
plainFields.description: Total available inventory immediately before this event. Used to reconstruct historical inventory state at any point in time. Combined with quantity_after, shows the exact change.

plainFields.name: quantity_after
plainFields.description: Total available inventory immediately after this event. The new inventory state after this event completed.

plainFields.name: quantity_changed
plainFields.description: Change amount (quantity_after - quantity_before). Positive for increases, negative for decreases. Enables quick analysis of inventory trends without calculation.

plainFields.name: reserved_before
plainFields.description: Reserved inventory quantity before this event. Tracks both available and reserved changes during order lifecycle.

plainFields.name: reserved_after
plainFields.description: Reserved inventory quantity after this event. Shows how this event affected reservations (orders placed create reservations, cancellations remove reservations).

plainFields.name: event_source
plainFields.description: Who or what triggered this inventory event. Valid values: 'customer_order' (customer placed order), 'seller_adjustment' (seller manually adjusted), 'admin_adjustment' (admin corrected), 'system_process' (automatic system process), 'return_process' (return fulfillment), 'order_cancellation' (automated cancellation).

plainFields.name: reference_id
plainFields.description: Reference identifier for tracking the event source. For order events, this is the order ID. For adjustments, this is the adjustment ID. For system processes, this is the process/job ID. Enables drilling down to specific business event.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Optional contextual notes about this inventory event. For example: 'Return received from customer, condition acceptable', 'Damage discovered during restock count', 'System correction after payment reversal'. Helps with investigation and troubleshooting.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this inventory event occurred and was recorded. Precise to the second. Enables timeline reconstruction and temporal queries.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_low_stock_alerts
models.description:
Alerts generated when product inventory falls below seller-configured thresholds. This table tracks low stock events and enables the notification system to alert sellers of depleting inventory.

When a product's available inventory decreases to or below the seller's configured low_stock_threshold, the system creates an alert record. Alerts trigger notifications to sellers via email, SMS, and in-app messaging to encourage timely reordering.

The table prevents alert fatigue by tracking alert history and limiting notification frequency (maximum one alert per SKU per day). It also tracks alert acknowledgment (when seller marks they're aware and reordering) and resolution (when inventory is restocked above threshold).

Low stock alerts are system-generated based on inventory changes, not created manually. Each alert is immutable once created (represents a point-in-time event). Alert history enables analysis of which products frequently run low on stock, indicating demand patterns or inventory planning issues.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the product variant with low inventory. References {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}. Each alert is specific to one SKU.

foreignFields.name: seller_id
foreignFields.description: Link to the seller who owns this inventory and will receive the low stock alert. References {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. Enables seller-specific alert tracking and notification delivery.

plainFields.name: current_stock
plainFields.description: Actual available inventory quantity when this low stock alert was created. The quantity that triggered the alert. Snapshot of inventory state at alert time (used for historical reference).

plainFields.name: threshold_level
plainFields.description: The seller's configured low stock threshold that was breached to trigger this alert. Recorded for audit trail (threshold may be changed by seller later).

plainFields.name: alert_status
plainFields.description: Current status of this alert. Valid values: 'active' (alert triggered, notifications sent, awaiting action), 'acknowledged' (seller confirmed aware and is reordering), 'resolved' (inventory restocked above threshold), 'snoozed' (seller temporarily suppressed alerts for 24 hours), 'dismissed' (seller marked as not concerning).

plainFields.name: notifications_sent
plainFields.description: Count of notifications sent for this alert (email, SMS, push, etc.). Tracks notification delivery volume. Limited to 1 notification per 24-hour period to prevent alert fatigue.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this low stock alert was automatically generated by the system (when inventory dropped to/below threshold).

plainFields.name: acknowledged_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when seller acknowledged this alert (if acknowledged). NULL if still awaiting acknowledgment. Used to track seller response time to alerts.

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when this alert was resolved (inventory restocked above threshold or alert manually resolved). NULL if still active or unresolved.

plainFields.name: last_notification_sent_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp of most recent notification sent for this alert. Used to enforce 24-hour notification frequency limit (don't spam seller with duplicate alerts for same SKU).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts
models.description:
Shopping cart storage for authenticated customers, maintaining temporary collections of products before checkout.

Stores the customer's current shopping cart with aggregated totals including subtotal, discounts, shipping estimates, and tax calculations. Each customer maintains one active cart that persists across sessions and devices. Cart state includes metadata for checkout flow such as selected shipping address, shipping method preference, and applied promotional codes.

Carts are not converted to orders in this table; instead, successful checkouts create separate order records in the order management system. Abandoned carts may exist indefinitely in the system but are marked with last_modified timestamps for analytics and recovery email campaigns.

Includes comprehensive totals for display (subtotal, estimated shipping, estimated tax, discount amount, grand total) and state tracking (whether address and shipping selections are finalized).

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who owns this cart. Each customer has exactly one active cart. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: subtotal_amount
plainFields.description: Sum of all line item subtotals (item price × quantity) before taxes, shipping, and discounts. Recalculated when cart items change.

plainFields.name: discount_amount
plainFields.description: Total discount amount applied through promotional codes or platform promotions. Stored separately for transparency.
