plainFields.name: estimated_shipping_amount
plainFields.description: Estimated shipping cost based on selected shipping address and shipping method. Recalculated if address or method changes.

plainFields.name: estimated_tax_amount
plainFields.description: Estimated tax calculated based on shipping destination address. Updated if address changes during checkout.

plainFields.name: grand_total_amount
plainFields.description: Final total including subtotal, discount, shipping, and tax. Used for display during checkout and payment authorization.

plainFields.name: item_count
plainFields.description: Denormalized count of cart items for quick display (shows number of products in cart). Incremented/decremented when items added/removed.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Cart status indicating its lifecycle state. Values: ACTIVE (customer shopping), ABANDONED (inactive 30+ days), CONVERTED (order placed). Used for analytics and recovery campaigns.

plainFields.name: promo_code_applied
plainFields.description: Promotional code or coupon code currently applied to this cart, if any. Stored for tracking and validation.

plainFields.name: selected_address_id
plainFields.description: UUID reference to the selected shipping address for this cart (denormalized for performance). Optional field; address may not be selected until checkout.

plainFields.name: selected_shipping_method
plainFields.description: Selected shipping method name (Standard, Express, Overnight, etc.). Null if not yet selected during checkout.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the shopping cart was created or first accessed by the customer.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to the cart (items added/removed, address/shipping updated).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_cart_items
models.description:
Individual line items stored within a shopping cart, representing specific product variants with quantity and pricing.

Each cart item represents one specific product variant (SKU) with denormalized price, quantity, and seller information captured at the time of addition to cart. Cart items maintain independent pricing records so that if a seller changes their product price after the item was added, the customer still sees the original price.

Cart items link to product_skus for inventory validation during checkout. Seller information is stored for display and multi-seller cart organization. When customers modify quantity or remove items, cart items are deleted entirely (no soft delete needed for ephemeral cart data).

Prices and totals are recalculated when quantities change, and line item subtotals are aggregated up to the parent cart's subtotal.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_shopping_cart_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent shopping cart that contains this item. {@link ecommerce_mall_shopping_carts.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the specific product variant (SKU) being added to cart. Links to inventory for stock validation. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller offering this product variant. Stored for multi-seller cart organization and fulfillment. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Number of units of this product variant in the cart. Must be positive integer. Limited to maximum 100 to prevent bulk buying abuse.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Price per unit captured at the time the item was added to cart. Frozen price independent of future seller price changes.

plainFields.name: line_total
plainFields.description: Calculated subtotal for this line item (unit_price × quantity). Recalculated when quantity changes.

plainFields.name: variant_details
plainFields.description: Denormalized description of selected variant attributes (e.g., 'Color: Blue, Size: Large, Width: Standard'). Used for display in cart.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this item was added to the shopping cart.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent modification to this cart item (quantity changed).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_wishlists
models.description:
Wishlist collections where customers save products they are interested in purchasing later, separate from shopping carts.

Allows customers to maintain one or more named wishlists (e.g., 'Summer Clothes', 'Gifts for Mom') for organizing products of interest. Wishlists are persistent across sessions and customer logins, used for price tracking, demand signals, and notifications when items are back in stock.

Wishlists can be marked as public to share with other customers via shareable links, or kept private for personal use only. Wishlist metadata includes whether it's public/private and visibility status. Multiple wishlists per customer enable organization by theme or recipient.

Contains aggregated count of items in the wishlist for display and reference. Timestamps track creation date and recent modifications.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who owns this wishlist. Customer can have multiple wishlists. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: User-friendly name for the wishlist (e.g., 'Summer Clothes', 'Birthday Gifts'). Max 255 characters for display in UI.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description of the wishlist's purpose or context. Helps customer organize and remember why items are grouped together.

plainFields.name: is_public
plainFields.description: Whether this wishlist is publicly shareable via link or kept private. Default false (private).

plainFields.name: item_count
plainFields.description: Denormalized count of items in this wishlist for quick display. Incremented/decremented when items added/removed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the wishlist was created by the customer.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent modification to the wishlist (items added/removed, visibility changed).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_wishlist_items
models.description:
Individual items saved in a customer's wishlist, representing product variants they are interested in for potential future purchase.

Each wishlist item represents one specific product variant (SKU) added to a wishlist without quantity selection (wishlists save single units of each variant, not quantities). Wishlist items store denormalized pricing and availability information captured at the time of addition for display purposes.

Wishlist items maintain independent reference to product SKUs for tracking availability and detecting when items come back in stock (triggering optional customer notifications). Seller information is stored to display which seller offers each wishlist item and their ratings.

Unlike cart items, wishlist items can be soft-deleted (marked with deleted_at) to preserve history while hiding items from active wishlist display. This supports recovery if customer wishes to restore accidentally removed items.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_wishlist_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the parent wishlist that contains this item. {@link ecommerce_mall_wishlists.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the specific product variant (SKU) saved in the wishlist. Used for availability and price tracking. {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller offering this product variant. Stored for display of seller information and ratings. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: price_at_add
plainFields.description: Product price captured at the time the item was added to the wishlist. Stored to show customer price changes (if current price differs).

plainFields.name: availability_at_add
plainFields.description: Availability status captured when item was added (In Stock, Low Stock, Out of Stock). Stored to detect availability changes.

plainFields.name: variant_details
plainFields.description: Denormalized description of the product variant attributes (e.g., 'Color: Blue, Size: Large'). Used for display in wishlist.

plainFields.name: notify_price_drop
plainFields.description: Whether customer wants to be notified if the price drops for this wishlist item. Default false (no notification).

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this item was added to the wishlist.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent modification to this wishlist item (notification preference changed).

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null if item is active in wishlist, set to deletion time if item was removed.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_orders
models.description:
Core order records representing committed customer purchases containing items from one or multiple sellers.

Each order captures a complete transaction from a customer including delivery address, shipping method selected, payment details, and overall order status. Orders are created when payment is successfully authorized and serve as the primary reference point for fulfillment, shipping, and customer order tracking.

Multi-seller orders are supported - a single order can contain items from different sellers, with each seller's items tracked separately in order_items table and fulfillment managed independently through order_fulfillments table.

Order status transitions through a defined lifecycle: pending → confirmed → processing → shipped → delivered → complete, with optional cancellation or refund states. Complete audit trail of all status changes is maintained in order_status_history table.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who placed the order. References {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_address_id
foreignFields.description: Delivery address for the order. References {@link ecommerce_mall_customer_addresses.id}.

plainFields.name: order_number
plainFields.description: Human-readable order identifier (e.g., ORD-2024-001234). Unique and displayed to customers for reference. This is the order number customers use to track and reference their order.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current order status in lifecycle. Valid values: pending, payment_processing, payment_failed, confirmed, processing, shipped, delivered, in_refund, refunded, complete, cancellation_pending, cancelled. Status determines what actions customers and sellers can take.

plainFields.name: subtotal_amount
plainFields.description: Sum of all order item prices before discounts, taxes, and shipping. Stored as precise decimal value in order currency.

plainFields.name: discount_amount
plainFields.description: Total discount applied from promo codes or promotions. Subtracted from subtotal to get discounted subtotal. Value is zero if no discount applied.

plainFields.name: tax_amount
plainFields.description: Calculated sales tax based on delivery address and applicable tax jurisdiction. Included in final order total.

plainFields.name: shipping_cost
plainFields.description: Shipping cost for the order. Locked in at checkout and not changed after order placement. May include regional surcharges or promotional free shipping.

plainFields.name: grand_total_amount
plainFields.description: Final order total: (subtotal - discount) + tax + shipping. This is the amount charged to customer. Calculation: subtotal_amount - discount_amount + tax_amount + shipping_cost.

plainFields.name: currency_code
plainFields.description: ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this order (e.g., USD, EUR, JPY). All prices recorded in this currency.

plainFields.name: shipping_method
plainFields.description: Shipping method selected by customer during checkout (e.g., standard, express, overnight). Determines delivery timeline and cost.

plainFields.name: estimated_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Estimated delivery date based on shipping method selected. Calculated at order time. Updated with actual delivery date when order is delivered.

plainFields.name: actual_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Actual delivery date when carrier confirms delivery. Set when order transitions to delivered status. Null until order is actually delivered.

plainFields.name: special_instructions
plainFields.description: Special delivery instructions from customer (e.g., leave at front door, ring doorbell twice). Optional customer notes for delivery handler.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when order was created (payment confirmed). Represents the point in time the order was placed and committed.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent order update. Updated whenever order status, items, or details change.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active orders. Set when order is deleted (for compliance, historical orders are soft-deleted not permanently removed).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_items
models.description:
Individual items within an order, representing specific product variants (SKUs) and quantities ordered.

When customers place orders containing items from multiple sellers, each item is a separate record in this table. This allows proper tracking of which items come from which sellers, enabling independent fulfillment by each seller.

Each order item captures the product details at time of order (price, variant specifications, seller information) to maintain historical accuracy. If product details change after order is placed, the order item retains the original details from order time.

Order items are referenced by fulfillment records which track seller-specific fulfillment status, allowing multiple sellers to independently manage their portion of the order.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order this item belongs to. References {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Specific product variant (SKU) ordered. References {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller providing this item. References {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. Allows identifying which seller fulfills this item.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_stock_reservation_id
foreignFields.description: Inventory reservation for this item. References {@link ecommerce_mall_stock_reservations.id}. Links to reserved stock tracking.

plainFields.name: product_name
plainFields.description: Product name at time of order (denormalized for historical accuracy). Stored in case product details are changed after order is placed.

plainFields.name: variant_description
plainFields.description: Description of product variant (color, size, options) selected for this item. Documents what specific variant was ordered.

plainFields.name: quantity
plainFields.description: Quantity of this item ordered. Positive integer, minimum 1 unit per order item.

plainFields.name: unit_price
plainFields.description: Price per unit at time of order (locked in). Quantity multiplied by unit_price equals line subtotal.

plainFields.name: line_total
plainFields.description: Total for this line item: quantity × unit_price. Contribution to order subtotal.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when item was added to order. Matches order creation time (items created with order).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_fulfillments
models.description:
Seller-specific fulfillment tracking for orders containing items from multiple sellers.

When an order contains items from multiple sellers, a separate fulfillment record is created for each seller. This allows each seller to independently manage their portion of the order - tracking items they need to fulfill, managing shipment, and updating delivery status.

Fulfillment records maintain seller-specific status (processing, shipped, delivered) independent from the main order status. This enables one seller to ship while another is still processing, with complete transparency to customer on per-seller fulfillment progress.

Each fulfillment contains all order items from that specific seller, referenced through order_items table. Shipment information is tracked through shipments table linked to fulfillments.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order this fulfillment is part of. References {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller responsible for fulfilling their items. References {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Fulfillment status from seller perspective. Valid values: pending, confirmed, preparing, ready_to_ship, shipped, delivered, cancelled. Tracks seller's progress fulfilling their items.

plainFields.name: item_count
plainFields.description: Number of order items from this seller in the order. Denormalized for quick reference of how many items seller needs to fulfill.

plainFields.name: fulfillment_deadline
plainFields.description: Expected date seller should ship order items. Based on order placement plus seller's configured processing time. Used to track SLA compliance.

plainFields.name: shipped_date
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller marked items as shipped. Set when seller confirms shipment and provides tracking number.

plainFields.name: delivered_date
plainFields.description: Timestamp when order items from this seller were confirmed delivered. Set from shipment tracking when carrier confirms delivery.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when fulfillment record was created (when order was confirmed). Marks when fulfillment begins for this seller.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent fulfillment status update.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipments
models.description:
Shipping records representing physical shipments of order fulfillments from sellers to customers.

Each shipment represents one physical package being sent by a seller (fulfillment). Shipments contain tracking information provided by the carrier and link to the shipping carrier's tracking system for real-time updates.

Multiple shipments can exist for a single order if different sellers ship from different locations or at different times. Each shipment has independent tracking and delivery status.

Shipment information is captured at time of shipment creation (carrier, tracking number, estimated delivery) and updated as carrier provides tracking events through shipment_tracking records.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_fulfillment_id
foreignFields.description: Order fulfillment this shipment is for. References {@link ecommerce_mall_order_fulfillments.id}.

plainFields.name: tracking_number
plainFields.description: Carrier's tracking number for this shipment. Used to retrieve tracking information from carrier's system. Unique per carrier but not globally unique.

plainFields.name: carrier_name
plainFields.description: Name of shipping carrier (FedEx, UPS, USPS, DHL, regional carriers, etc.). Identifies which carrier's tracking system to query.

plainFields.name: estimated_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Estimated delivery date provided by carrier at shipment time. Based on carrier's service level and destination. Updated as carrier provides new estimates.

plainFields.name: actual_delivery_date
plainFields.description: Actual delivery confirmation date from carrier tracking. Set when carrier confirms delivery. Null until item is delivered.

plainFields.name: last_tracking_update
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent tracking event from carrier. Indicates freshness of tracking information.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current shipment status from carrier. Values: in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, exception, lost, returned. Reflects carrier's last reported status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when shipment record was created (when seller marked items as shipped).

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent shipment update. Updated as tracking information is received from carrier.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_tracking
models.description:
Historical tracking events for shipments, capturing each status update from carrier.

As shipments move through the carrier's system, they generate tracking events (picked up, in transit, out for delivery, delivered, etc.). Each event is recorded here with timestamp and event details for complete visibility into shipment journey.

Tracking events are received from carrier APIs or webhooks and stored chronologically. This creates audit trail of shipment progression and enables reconstructing complete delivery timeline.

Each tracking event includes carrier-provided information such as location, status, and any delivery exceptions or special events.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_shipment_id
foreignFields.description: Shipment this tracking event is for. References {@link ecommerce_mall_shipments.id}.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Type of tracking event (picked_up, in_transit, arrival_at_facility, out_for_delivery, delivery_attempted, delivered, exception, returned). Indicates what happened to shipment.

plainFields.name: event_timestamp
plainFields.description: When the tracking event occurred according to carrier. This is the actual event time, not when it was reported to our system.

plainFields.name: location
plainFields.description: Location where event occurred (city, facility name, or address). Optional, not all carriers provide detailed location info.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Human-readable description of tracking event from carrier. Example: 'Package picked up' or 'Out for delivery today'.

plainFields.name: exception_reason
plainFields.description: If event type is exception, reason for exception (address issue, delivery failed, weather delay, etc.). Null for non-exception events.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this tracking event was recorded in our system (when we received update from carrier).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_order_status_history
models.description:
Audit trail recording all order status transitions throughout order lifecycle.

Every time an order's status changes, a history record is created documenting the transition. This maintains complete history of how order progressed from creation through completion or cancellation.

Status history enables reconstructing the complete order timeline, investigating why orders are in particular states, and tracking when key milestones occurred (when payment was confirmed, when seller started processing, when order was shipped, when delivered).

Each history record includes the status change, timestamp, and reason/notes explaining why the change occurred (automatic system transition, customer cancellation request, seller action, admin intervention, etc.).

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order whose status changed. References {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description: Status before this transition. Null for initial order creation (no previous status).

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description: Status after this transition. The status the order moved to.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for status change. Examples: 'Payment authorized', 'Customer cancellation request', 'Seller marked shipped', 'Carrier delivered', 'Return approved'.

plainFields.name: initiated_by
plainFields.description: Who/what initiated the status change. Values: 'system' (automatic transition), 'customer', 'seller', 'admin', 'carrier' (tracking update).

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description: Additional context or notes about the status change. Optional field for capturing extra information about transition.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when status transition occurred.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_transactions
models.description:
Core payment transaction records tracking all payment processing attempts and their outcomes. Records the complete lifecycle of a customer payment from initiation through completion or failure.

Each transaction represents a single payment attempt for an order or partial order. Transactions are immutable once created and include complete details of the payment including amount, method, processor response, and authorization codes.

Transactions link to orders and payment methods, enabling tracking of which payment method was used and what order it paid for. Status field tracks workflow (pending → processing → authorized → completed or failed). Soft deletion preserves all payment history for compliance and audit purposes.

The transaction table is the source of truth for all financial records and integrates with seller settlements for commission calculations and payment distributions.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order being paid for. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_method_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the payment method used (credit card, debit card, digital wallet, etc.). {@link ecommerce_mall_payment_methods.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer who initiated the payment. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: transaction_reference_id
plainFields.description: Unique transaction reference from payment processor (e.g., Stripe transaction ID, PayPal transaction ID). Used for tracking and reconciliation with payment processor.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current transaction status. Valid values: pending (awaiting processing), processing (payment is being processed), authorized (payment authorized but not yet settled), completed (payment successfully completed and settled), failed (payment failed), cancelled (transaction cancelled by user or system), refunded (payment refunded to customer). Determines which operations are allowed on the transaction.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Amount charged to customer in the transaction currency. Must be a positive number with maximum 2 decimal places. This is the gross amount including all fees.

plainFields.name: currency_code
plainFields.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the transaction (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Determines how amount is interpreted and enables multi-currency support.

plainFields.name: payment_method_type
plainFields.description: Type of payment method used. Valid values: credit_card, debit_card, digital_wallet (Apple Pay, Google Pay), bank_transfer, paypal, bnpl (Buy Now Pay Later), other. Helps categorize payments for analytics and compliance.

plainFields.name: processor_name
plainFields.description: Name of the payment processor handling the transaction (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, Square, Adyen). Identifies which processor handled the payment for troubleshooting and reconciliation.

plainFields.name: processor_response_code
plainFields.description: Response code from payment processor indicating the authorization result. Examples: 200 (success), 400 (bad request), 402 (payment required), 403 (forbidden), 429 (rate limited), 500 (server error). Used for error handling and debugging.

plainFields.name: processor_response_message
plainFields.description: Human-readable response message from payment processor explaining the result. Examples: 'Card approved', 'Insufficient funds', 'Invalid card', 'Declined by bank'. Shown to customer to explain transaction outcome.

plainFields.name: authorization_code
plainFields.description: Authorization code returned by payment processor for approved transactions. Used to settle (capture) the payment and for processor reconciliation. Required for completed transactions.

plainFields.name: risk_score
plainFields.description: Fraud risk score from payment processor (0-100 scale where 0=low risk, 100=high risk). Used for fraud detection and triggering additional verification steps. Scores above 75 may trigger manual review.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address of the customer making the payment. Used for fraud detection, geographic verification, and security auditing. Stored for compliance investigation.

plainFields.name: retry_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this payment has been retried by the system. Starts at 0 for first attempt. System may automatically retry failed payments up to 2 times. Helps prevent duplicate charges by tracking retry attempts.

plainFields.name: settled_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment was settled (funds captured from customer account). Empty for pending or failed transactions. For completed transactions, this marks when funds actually moved.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the transaction was initiated. Marks the start of the payment lifecycle.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last status update or modification to the transaction. Tracks when transaction state last changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active transactions. When set, indicates transaction has been logically deleted while preserving audit trail. Compliance requirement for 7-year payment retention.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_failures
models.description:
Detailed records of payment processing failures and their error details. Tracks every failed payment attempt to enable root cause analysis, retry mechanisms, and compliance reporting.

When a payment transaction fails (is declined, times out, or returns an error), a failure record is created capturing the specific error code, message, and context. This enables the system to understand why payments fail and take appropriate action (retry, notify customer, escalate to support).

Failure records link to the associated payment transaction and maintain complete error information from the payment processor. They support the automatic retry system and fraud detection mechanisms.

The failure table is subsidiary to payment transactions - it exists only to supplement transaction records with failure-specific details. Failures are immutable once created and preserved for PCI compliance and audit purposes.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the payment transaction that failed. {@link ecommerce_mall_payment_transactions.id}.

plainFields.name: error_code
plainFields.description: Error code from payment processor identifying the type of failure. Examples: insufficient_funds, card_declined, expired_card, invalid_cvv, processing_error, timeout, rate_limited. Used to categorize failures for analysis and automated remediation.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Human-readable error message from payment processor explaining the failure. Examples: 'Your card was declined', 'Your card has expired', 'Payment processor is temporarily unavailable'. Shown to customer to explain payment failure.

plainFields.name: failure_category
plainFields.description: Categorization of failure type: temporary (transient issue that may succeed on retry), permanent (customer action required), processor_error (payment processor issue). Used to determine retry strategy and customer notification.

plainFields.name: processor_raw_response
plainFields.description: Complete raw response from payment processor including all fields and metadata. Stored for debugging and compliance purposes. Helps investigate complex failures.

plainFields.name: retry_scheduled
plainFields.description: Whether system has automatically scheduled a retry of this payment. Temporary failures may be automatically retried. This flag indicates if retry is planned.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the payment failure was recorded. Marks when the failure occurred.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active failure records. When set, indicates failure has been logically deleted. Soft delete preserves audit trail for compliance.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_requests
models.description:
Customer or system-initiated refund requests for completed payments. Records the intention to refund an order or partial order and tracks the approval/denial workflow.

Refund requests capture the business context for why a refund is needed: customer initiated return, system-detected issue, seller non-shipment, or damage claim. They represent the customer's intent to get money back and guide the refund processing workflow.

Each request has independent status tracking (pending, approved, rejected, processing, completed) enabling management of the refund lifecycle separate from the original payment. Refund requests can reference the original payment transaction and associated order.

This is a primary table because refund requests are independently managed through a complete workflow, not merely attached to another entity. Customers can submit refund requests, they can be approved/denied, and they trigger actual payment reversals (refunds table).

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the order for which refund is being requested. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original payment transaction being refunded. {@link ecommerce_mall_payment_transactions.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer requesting the refund. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund request. Valid values: pending (awaiting approval), approved (approved and ready for processing), rejected (denied, no refund will be issued), processing (refund is being processed), completed (refund successfully processed and paid to customer), failed (refund processing failed). Tracks workflow progress.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Reason for the refund request from the customer or system. Valid values: customer_initiated (customer requested refund), damaged_item (item arrived damaged), defective_product (product doesn't work as described), wrong_item (order contained wrong item), no_shipment (seller didn't ship), seller_issue (seller service issue), payment_error (system charged incorrect amount), fraud_dispute (customer disputes the charge). Used to understand refund patterns.

plainFields.name: requested_amount
plainFields.description: Amount customer is requesting to be refunded. Must be a positive number not exceeding the original order amount. For partial refunds, this is less than full order. Decimal with 2 places maximum.

plainFields.name: approved_amount
plainFields.description: Amount actually approved for refund after review. May differ from requested amount (e.g., restocking fee applied, partial refund approved). Null until request is reviewed.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for rejecting the refund request if status is rejected. Examples: outside_return_window, item_condition_unacceptable, duplicate_request, no_supporting_evidence. Explains why refund was denied.

plainFields.name: customer_notes
plainFields.description: Detailed notes from customer explaining why they want a refund. May include description of damage, product issues, or other context supporting the request. Max 2000 characters.

plainFields.name: admin_notes
plainFields.description: Internal notes from admin or support team during refund review. May include investigation findings, decision rationale, or customer communication details. Not visible to customer.

plainFields.name: requested_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the customer submitted the refund request. Marks the start of the refund request lifecycle.

plainFields.name: reviewed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request was reviewed and approved/rejected. Null while request is pending. Marks when decision was made.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund request record was created in the system. Should match requested_at in most cases.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the refund request (approval, status change, notes added, etc). Tracks when request state last changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active refund requests. When set, indicates request has been logically deleted. Soft deletion preserves audit trail for compliance.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_refunds
models.description:
Processed refunds representing actual payment reversals to customer accounts. Records the complete lifecycle of refund transactions from approval through settlement.

When a refund request is approved, a refund record is created capturing the refund transaction details. The refund tracks the actual reversal of funds to the customer's original payment method (or alternative method if necessary).

Each refund maintains complete transaction data including amount, currency, processor reference, and status throughout the reversal process. Refunds may be processed immediately or may take several business days depending on the payment method and processor.

The refund table is subsidiary to refund requests - it exists to implement the approved refund through actual payment reversal. Refunds are immutable once created and preserved for complete financial audit trail and compliance with 7-year payment retention requirements.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_refund_request_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the refund request that triggered this refund. {@link ecommerce_mall_refund_requests.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_transaction_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the original payment transaction being refunded. {@link ecommerce_mall_payment_transactions.id}.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the refund processing. Valid values: processing (refund initiated, awaiting processor confirmation), completed (refund successfully processed and funds returned to customer), failed (refund processing failed, requires retry or manual intervention), cancelled (refund was cancelled before completion). Tracks refund lifecycle.

plainFields.name: refund_amount
plainFields.description: Amount being refunded to customer. Must be a positive number with maximum 2 decimal places. May be less than original payment for partial refunds or if restocking fees applied.

plainFields.name: currency_code
plainFields.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the refund (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP). Should match the original payment transaction currency.

plainFields.name: processor_refund_id
plainFields.description: Unique refund transaction ID from payment processor (e.g., Stripe refund ID). Used to track refund status with processor and reconcile payments. Critical for processor communication.

plainFields.name: processor_name
plainFields.description: Name of the payment processor handling the refund (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, Square). Should match the original transaction processor.

plainFields.name: refund_method
plainFields.description: How the refund is being issued. Valid values: original_payment_method (refunded to original card/payment method), bank_transfer (direct bank transfer), store_credit (issued as store credit balance), check (issued as physical check). Determines where funds go.

plainFields.name: expected_completion_date
plainFields.description: Estimated date when customer will see refund in their account. Varies by payment method (2-5 business days typical). Communicated to customer for expectation setting.

plainFields.name: actual_completion_date
plainFields.description: Actual date when refund was confirmed complete and funds returned to customer. Set when processor confirms completion. Null while processing.

plainFields.name: processor_response_code
plainFields.description: Response code from payment processor for the refund request. Examples: 200 (success), 400 (bad request), 422 (unprocessable), 500 (server error). Used for debugging refund failures.

plainFields.name: processor_response_message
plainFields.description: Human-readable message from processor explaining the refund result. Examples: 'Refund successfully submitted', 'Original transaction not found', 'Refund amount exceeds original'. Helps explain refund status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the refund was initiated. Marks when the refund processing began.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last status update or modification to the refund. Tracks when refund state last changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active refunds. When set, indicates refund has been logically deleted. Soft deletion preserves audit trail for 7-year compliance requirement.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_settlements
models.description:
Seller commission calculations and payment settlement records. Tracks the financial settlement between the platform and sellers for their sales.

Seller settlements aggregate payment transactions across a settlement period (weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly based on seller preference) and calculate the net amount owed to the seller after deducting platform commissions and fees.

Each settlement record captures the complete financial picture: total gross sales, commission amount deducted, any adjustments or chargebacks, and the final net settlement amount to be paid to the seller. Settlements drive the actual payments made to sellers via their configured bank accounts.

This is a primary table because settlements represent critical financial records independently tracked for each seller. Settlements are primary business entities that drive seller payments, require comprehensive tracking, and need detailed analytics and reporting.

Settlements maintain immutable records of all historical settlements for each seller, enabling complete financial audit trails and enabling sellers to understand their earnings over time.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller this settlement is for. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}.

plainFields.name: settlement_period_start
plainFields.description: Start date of the settlement period (date from which sales are included). All transactions on or after this date are included in settlement calculations.

plainFields.name: settlement_period_end
plainFields.description: End date of the settlement period (last date on which sales are included). All transactions before this date are included in settlement calculations.

plainFields.name: settlement_frequency
plainFields.description: Frequency of settlement for this seller. Valid values: weekly (every 7 days), biweekly (every 14 days), monthly (once per month). Set by seller's preference and controls when settlements are calculated.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current status of the settlement. Valid values: pending (calculated but not yet paid), processing (payment in progress), completed (payment successfully made to seller), failed (payment failed and requires retry or manual intervention), cancelled (settlement was cancelled without payment). Tracks settlement lifecycle.

plainFields.name: gross_sales_amount
plainFields.description: Total gross sales amount before commission deduction. Sum of all transaction amounts from the settlement period for this seller. Decimal with 2 places maximum.

plainFields.name: commission_percentage
plainFields.description: Commission rate applied as percentage (e.g., 15.5 for 15.5%). The rate may vary by product category. This is the rate applied to calculate commission_amount.

plainFields.name: commission_amount
plainFields.description: Total commission deducted from gross sales (calculated as gross_sales_amount × commission_percentage / 100). This is the platform's fee.

plainFields.name: chargebacks_and_disputes
plainFields.description: Total amount deducted due to chargebacks, disputes, or customer complaints. These represent costs to the seller for disputed transactions. Default 0 if no disputes.

plainFields.name: refunds_issued
plainFields.description: Total amount of refunds issued during the settlement period for this seller's products. Refunds reduce the net settlement amount owed to seller.

plainFields.name: other_adjustments
plainFields.description: Any other adjustments to the settlement (credits, penalties, bonuses, etc). Can be positive (credit to seller) or negative (deduction from seller). Includes manual adjustments made by admin.

plainFields.name: net_settlement_amount
plainFields.description: Final net amount to be paid to seller after all deductions and adjustments. Calculated as: gross_sales_amount - commission_amount - chargebacks_and_disputes - refunds_issued + other_adjustments. This is what seller actually receives.

plainFields.name: currency_code
plainFields.description: ISO 4217 currency code for settlement amounts (e.g., USD, EUR). Should match seller's preferred settlement currency.

plainFields.name: payment_method
plainFields.description: Method used to pay the seller. Valid values: bank_transfer (direct to seller's bank account), check (mailed check), paypal (PayPal transfer), cryptocurrency (crypto transfer). Determined by seller's payment preferences.

plainFields.name: payment_reference_id
plainFields.description: Reference ID for the actual payment transaction (e.g., bank transfer ID, check number, PayPal transaction ID). Null until payment is completed.

plainFields.name: calculated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the settlement was calculated and amounts determined. Marks when settlement figures were finalized.

plainFields.name: paid_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the settlement payment was actually made to the seller's account. Null until payment completes. Marks when seller receives their money.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the settlement record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp of the last update to the settlement (status change, payment made, adjustment applied, etc). Tracks when settlement state last changed.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. Null for active settlements. When set, indicates settlement has been logically deleted. Soft deletion preserves audit trail for compliance and seller financial records.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_reviews
models.description:
Customer product reviews and ratings system.

Stores product reviews submitted by customers who have verified purchases. Each review contains a rating (1-5 stars), detailed review text, and category-specific dimension ratings. Reviews go through moderation workflow before publication and can be edited or deleted by the reviewer. Soft deletion is supported for moderation needs.

Reviews are independently managed - customers can search reviews across products, moderate reviews across the platform, and engage in review moderation workflows independent of the products themselves. This makes reviews a primary entity requiring direct CRUD operations.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Verified customer who submitted the review. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Product being reviewed. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Order containing the purchased product being reviewed. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}. Establishes verified purchase connection.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: Specific product variant (SKU) being reviewed. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}. Enables SKU-specific feedback.

plainFields.name: rating
plainFields.description: Overall product rating on 1-5 star scale. Range: 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Mandatory for all reviews.

plainFields.name: overall_quality_rating
plainFields.description: Rating for overall product quality on 1-5 scale. Part of dimension-specific ratings for analytics.

plainFields.name: matches_description_rating
plainFields.description: Rating for product matching seller's description on 1-5 scale. Critical for identifying misleading listings.

plainFields.name: value_for_money_rating
plainFields.description: Rating for product value relative to price on 1-5 scale. Helps customers assess pricing fairness.

plainFields.name: overall_satisfaction_rating
plainFields.description: Overall satisfaction rating on 1-5 scale. General customer satisfaction metric.

plainFields.name: category_specific_rating
plainFields.description: Category-specific dimension rating (e.g., fit for apparel, performance for electronics) on 1-5 scale. Varies by product category.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Review title summarizing the review in 50-150 characters. Appears in search results and review lists.

plainFields.name: body
plainFields.description: Detailed review text (minimum 20 characters, maximum 5000 characters). Contains customer's detailed experience and assessment.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Review moderation status. Valid values: pending (awaiting moderation), approved (published), rejected (not published), unlisted (hidden after publishing). Controls review visibility to customers.

plainFields.name: quality_score
plainFields.description: Automated quality score (0-100) based on completeness, authenticity, and relevance. Used for moderation prioritization and fraud detection.

plainFields.name: authenticity_score
plainFields.description: Authenticity score (0-100) calculated from verified purchase status, reviewer history, and fraud indicators. Identifies potentially fraudulent reviews.

plainFields.name: helpful_votes_up
plainFields.description: Number of customers who marked review as helpful. Starts at 0, incremented as customers vote. Used for review ranking.

plainFields.name: helpful_votes_down
plainFields.description: Number of customers who marked review as not helpful. Starts at 0. If significantly exceeds helpful votes, review may be delisted.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when review was published/approved. Null if review not yet approved. Enables review freshness tracking.

plainFields.name: days_since_purchase
plainFields.description: Number of days between order delivery and review submission. Used for authenticity scoring (ideal: 7-180 days).

plainFields.name: reviewer_name_display
plainFields.description: Display name for reviewer (customer's name or 'Anonymous'). Allows customers to hide identity while maintaining verified purchase badge.

plainFields.name: is_verified_purchase
plainFields.description: Whether review is from verified customer purchase. True if customer actually purchased the product. Critical for authenticity.

plainFields.name: is_anonymous
plainFields.description: Whether reviewer chose to post anonymously. True hides reviewer name but keeps verified purchase badge.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Review submission timestamp. Used for sorting (most recent first) and calculating review age.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp (edit, status change, moderation action). Tracks review modification history.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp for reviews removed by moderator or author. Null if review not deleted. Preserves review history.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_responses
models.description:
Seller responses to customer product reviews.

Allows sellers to respond to customer reviews with contextual information, problem resolution, or clarification. Each review can have maximum one seller response, implementing 1:1 relationship via unique constraint on review_id. Response goes through basic moderation to prevent abuse. Responses help sellers engage with customer feedback and address concerns.

Responses are subsidiary - managed through parent review and not independently searched or managed by customers. Sellers access responses through their product reviews.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_review_id
foreignFields.description: Parent review being responded to. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_product_reviews.id}. Establishes 1:1 relationship.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller providing the response. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. Enables seller management of responses.

plainFields.name: response_text
plainFields.description: Seller's response to the review (maximum 1000 characters). Professional, factual response addressing customer concerns or providing context.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Response moderation status. Valid values: pending (awaiting moderation), approved (published), rejected (not published). Prevents abusive responses.

plainFields.name: response_type
plainFields.description: Type of response: acknowledgment (thank you), clarification (additional context), resolution (problem solved), apology (acknowledgment of issue). Helps categorize seller engagement.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Response submission timestamp. Used for sorting responses chronologically.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for response edits. Tracks modification history.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp if response is removed. Null if response not deleted. Preserves history.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_moderation
models.description:
Review moderation workflow tracking and decision records.

Tracks the complete moderation lifecycle for each review including submission, manual review, approval/rejection decisions, and appeals. Each review has one moderation record controlling its visibility to customers. Records moderator decisions with reasons and timestamps for compliance and audit purposes.

Moderation is subsidiary - system-maintained through reviews with no independent customer management. Supports admin oversight of content quality.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_review_id
foreignFields.description: Review being moderated. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_product_reviews.id}. One moderation record per review.

foreignFields.name: moderated_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who moderated the review. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}. Null if auto-approved. Tracks human moderation.

plainFields.name: risk_level
plainFields.description: Moderation risk classification: low (auto-approved), medium (manual review), high (priority review). Determines moderation priority.

plainFields.name: moderation_decision
plainFields.description: Moderation outcome: auto_approved (automated approval), approved (manual approval), rejected (not published), unlisted (hidden after publish). Controls review visibility.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description: Reason for rejection if moderation_decision is 'rejected'. Values: policy_violation, offensive_content, spam, fraudulent, off_topic, low_quality, duplicate. Guides reviewer correction.

plainFields.name: moderation_notes
plainFields.description: Moderator's internal notes about the review (maximum 1000 characters). Additional context or flags for future review.

plainFields.name: content_flags
plainFields.description: Comma-separated flags detected in review: profanity, spam_patterns, fraud_indicators, contact_info, competitor_ref. Used for automated flagging.

plainFields.name: flag_spam_score
plainFields.description: Spam detection score (0-100). Higher indicates more likely spam. Used for automated flagging.

plainFields.name: flag_fraud_score
plainFields.description: Fraud detection score (0-100). Higher indicates more likely fraudulent review. Used for authenticity assessment.

plainFields.name: appeal_submitted
plainFields.description: Whether reviewer appealed moderation decision. True if appeal exists. Enables appeal workflow.

plainFields.name: appeal_notes
plainFields.description: Reviewer's appeal explanation (maximum 1000 characters). Justification for why decision should be reversed.

plainFields.name: appeal_decision
plainFields.description: Appeal outcome: pending (awaiting review), approved (appeal accepted), denied (appeal rejected). Null if no appeal submitted.

plainFields.name: moderation_timestamp
plainFields.description: When moderation decision was made. Used for SLA tracking and audit.

plainFields.name: appeal_timestamp
plainFields.description: When appeal was submitted. Null if no appeal. Tracks appeal timing.

plainFields.name: appeal_resolved_timestamp
plainFields.description: When appeal was resolved. Null if appeal pending or not submitted. Tracks appeal completion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Moderation record creation timestamp. Set when review is submitted.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for moderation record. Changes when decision made or appeal resolved.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_review_media
models.description:
Images and media attached to customer product reviews.

Stores references to photos and videos customers attach to reviews for visual evidence (product condition, quality, usage). Supports up to 5 images per review. Images are stored on CDN and referenced by URL. Enables visual feedback that helps other customers understand product quality.

Review media is subsidiary - managed through parent review and not independently managed by customers.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_review_id
foreignFields.description: Parent review containing this media. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_product_reviews.id}. Multiple media items per review allowed.

plainFields.name: media_type
plainFields.description: Type of media: image (JPEG/PNG), video. Determines how media is displayed and processed.

plainFields.name: media_url
plainFields.description: URL to media stored on CDN. https:// URL pointing to optimized media. Enables fast delivery from global CDN.

plainFields.name: thumbnail_url
plainFields.description: URL to thumbnail version for display in lists. Smaller version for faster loading in review listings.

plainFields.name: original_filename
plainFields.description: Original filename uploaded by customer. Preserved for audit trail and debugging.

plainFields.name: file_size_bytes
plainFields.description: Size of original media file in bytes. Used for bandwidth tracking and quota management.

plainFields.name: width_pixels
plainFields.description: Image width in pixels. Used for responsive display and CDN optimization.

plainFields.name: height_pixels
plainFields.description: Image height in pixels. Used for responsive display.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Order of display in review (1, 2, 3, etc.). Allows customers to control image sequence.

plainFields.name: is_moderated
plainFields.description: Whether media was reviewed by moderator. True if image passed content filtering (no violation). Tracks moderation status.

plainFields.name: moderation_status
plainFields.description: Media moderation status: pending (awaiting review), approved (no issues), rejected (violates policy). Controls display.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Media upload timestamp. Used for sorting media chronologically.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for media metadata. Changes when moderation status updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft deletion timestamp if media removed. Null if media not deleted. Preserves history.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_ratings
models.description:
Aggregated seller performance ratings across all orders.

Calculates composite seller rating based on customer feedback dimensions: seller communication, shipping speed, accuracy, and overall satisfaction. One rating record per seller aggregating all customer feedback for that seller. Ratings determine seller badges (Top Seller, Trusted Seller) and influence search ranking.

Seller ratings are subsidiary - computed from reviews and displayed read-only to customers. Sellers cannot directly manage ratings.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller being rated. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. One rating record per seller.

plainFields.name: composite_rating
plainFields.description: Overall seller rating on 1-5 scale with 1 decimal precision (e.g., 4.3). Calculated from weighted average of dimension ratings. Displayed prominently on seller profile.

plainFields.name: seller_communication_rating
plainFields.description: Average communication responsiveness rating (1-5 scale). How quickly seller responds to customer inquiries.

plainFields.name: shipping_speed_rating
plainFields.description: Average shipping speed rating (1-5 scale). How quickly seller ships orders from confirmation.

plainFields.name: seller_accuracy_rating
plainFields.description: Average accuracy rating (1-5 scale). How accurately seller fulfills orders (correct items, quantity, condition).

plainFields.name: item_description_accuracy_rating
plainFields.description: Average description accuracy rating (1-5 scale). How well product descriptions match actual items received.

plainFields.name: review_count
plainFields.description: Total number of customer reviews for this seller. Higher count = more reliable rating. Used for badge qualification.

plainFields.name: positive_feedback_percentage
plainFields.description: Percentage of orders with positive customer feedback (4-5 stars). Target: 90%+. Indicates customer satisfaction.

plainFields.name: return_rate_percentage
plainFields.description: Percentage of seller's orders that were returned. Lower is better. Target: <5%. Indicates product quality.

plainFields.name: on_time_delivery_percentage
plainFields.description: Percentage of orders delivered on or before estimated date. Target: 95%+. Indicates reliability.

plainFields.name: seller_badge
plainFields.description: Seller quality badge: top_seller (4.6+★, 200+ reviews, 95%+ positive), trusted_seller (4.3+★, 100+ reviews, 90%+ positive), verified_seller (email verified), new_seller (< 30 days), none. Displayed on store and products.

plainFields.name: days_on_platform
plainFields.description: Number of days since seller joined platform. Used for new seller identification and trust assessment.

plainFields.name: total_orders_sold
plainFields.description: Cumulative number of orders fulfilled by this seller. High count indicates experience and scale.

plainFields.name: total_reviews_received
plainFields.description: Total number of distinct customer reviews. Higher count makes rating more statistically significant.

plainFields.name: average_response_hours
plainFields.description: Average hours for seller to respond to customer inquiries. Lower is better. Used for communication rating.

plainFields.name: last_rating_update
plainFields.description: Timestamp of most recent rating calculation. Updated daily. Ensures freshness of displayed ratings.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Seller rating record creation timestamp. Set when seller first gets a review.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Last update timestamp for rating record. Updates when new reviews are published or calculation occurs.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_rating_metrics
models.description:
Time-series seller rating metrics for trend analysis and historical tracking.

Stores daily snapshots of seller ratings to track rating trends over time (improving, declining, stable). Enables identification of sudden rating changes and long-term performance trends. Supports seller performance analytics and business intelligence reporting.

Rating metrics are subsidiary - calculated from reviews and used for analytics only. Not directly managed by users.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Seller whose metrics are recorded. Reference to {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}. Multiple time-series records per seller.

plainFields.name: metric_date
plainFields.description: Date of metric snapshot (typically daily at midnight UTC). Enables time-series charting.

plainFields.name: composite_rating
plainFields.description: Seller's composite rating on this date (1-5 scale). Captured for trend tracking.

plainFields.name: seller_communication_rating
plainFields.description: Communication rating on this date. Tracks trend in communication responsiveness.

plainFields.name: shipping_speed_rating
plainFields.description: Shipping speed rating on this date. Tracks trend in fulfillment speed.

plainFields.name: seller_accuracy_rating
plainFields.description: Accuracy rating on this date. Tracks trend in order accuracy.

plainFields.name: item_description_accuracy_rating
plainFields.description: Description accuracy rating on this date. Tracks trend in listing quality.

plainFields.name: review_count
plainFields.description: Total reviews on this date. Tracks how review volume grows.

plainFields.name: positive_feedback_percentage
plainFields.description: Positive feedback percentage on this date. Tracks satisfaction trend.

plainFields.name: return_rate_percentage
plainFields.description: Return rate on this date. Tracks quality trend.

plainFields.name: on_time_delivery_percentage
plainFields.description: On-time delivery percentage on this date. Tracks reliability trend.

plainFields.name: total_orders_sold
plainFields.description: Cumulative orders on this date. Tracks seller growth.

plainFields.name: average_response_hours
plainFields.description: Average response time on this date. Tracks communication speed trend.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Record creation timestamp (when snapshot was taken). Set at metric calculation time.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_support_categories
models.description:
Support ticket and knowledge base article categories for organizing support content.

Provides hierarchical categorization system for support tickets, knowledge base articles, and FAQ items. Enables customers and support agents to browse and filter support content by topic areas such as shipping, returns, product quality, payment issues, etc.

Categories can be nested (parent-child hierarchy) for detailed organization. Each category tracks creation timestamps and supports soft deletion for audit compliance. Categories remain available even after soft deletion to maintain historical integrity of categorized items.

foreignFields.name: parent_id
foreignFields.description: Parent category for hierarchical organization. Allows self-referencing for nested category structures. {@link ecommerce_mall_support_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description: Category name displayed to customers and support staff. Examples: 'Shipping & Delivery', 'Returns & Refunds', 'Product Quality', 'Payment Issues'. Unique within each category level.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: URL-friendly slug for category identification. Used in support portal URLs. Examples: 'shipping-delivery', 'returns-refunds'. Lowercase with hyphens.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the support category explaining what types of issues it covers. Displayed to customers when browsing support topics.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Sort order for displaying categories to users. Lower numbers appear first in category listings.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description: Whether this category is active and visible to customers. Inactive categories are hidden from support portals but historical associations are preserved.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the support category was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the support category was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, category is marked as deleted but retained in database for audit trail and historical reference.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_support_tickets
models.description:
Customer support tickets capturing inquiries, issues, and service requests.

Core entity for the support system. Customers create tickets when they need assistance with orders, products, shipping, returns, or general platform issues. Each ticket is assigned a unique ticket number for customer reference and tracking.

Tickets progress through status workflow: open → in_progress → resolved → closed. Support agents are assigned to tickets and can leave messages and internal notes. Tickets are categorized by support category and linked to relevant orders when applicable. System tracks priority level, allowing urgent issues to be addressed first.

Tickets support full soft deletion for compliance while maintaining historical records. Created and updated timestamps enable SLA tracking and support performance monitoring.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who created this support ticket. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Associated order if ticket is related to a specific order. May be null for general inquiries. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_support_category_id
foreignFields.description: Support category this ticket belongs to. Enables routing to appropriate support team. {@link ecommerce_mall_support_categories.id}.

foreignFields.name: assigned_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin user assigned to handle this ticket. Null if unassigned. {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: ticket_number
plainFields.description: Unique human-readable ticket identifier for customer reference. Format: TICKET-YYYYMMDD-NNNN. Example: TICKET-20240115-0042.

plainFields.name: subject
plainFields.description: Brief subject line summarizing the customer's issue. Examples: 'Order not received', 'Wrong item shipped', 'Quality concern with product'.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the customer's issue or inquiry. May include problem context, screenshots, or specific details needed for resolution.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Current ticket status. Values: open (new, unassigned), in_progress (being handled), resolved (solution provided), closed (completed). Drives workflow routing.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description: Priority level affecting response time. Values: low, normal, high, urgent. Urgent issues get immediate attention. Supports SLA tracking.

plainFields.name: is_internal_note
plainFields.description: Flag indicating if this ticket contains internal notes/communication. Internal tickets are not visible to customers in their support portal.

plainFields.name: resolution_notes
plainFields.description: Notes from support agent describing how the ticket was resolved. Populated when status changes to resolved or closed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the support ticket was created by customer.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the support ticket was last updated (message added, status changed, reassigned).

plainFields.name: resolved_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when ticket was marked as resolved. Used for SLA tracking and response time metrics.

plainFields.name: closed_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when ticket was closed. After closure, no new messages can be added unless ticket is reopened.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, ticket is marked as deleted but retained in database for historical reference and compliance.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_support_ticket_messages
models.description:
Conversation messages within support tickets creating communication thread.

Captures all communication between customer and support agents on a specific ticket. Each message is timestamped and attributed to the creator (customer or admin). Messages form the conversation history and context for ticket resolution.

Supports both customer-visible messages and internal support team notes marked as internal. Messages cannot be edited after creation (immutable for audit compliance) but can be soft-deleted if inappropriate or accidental.

Messages are essential for maintaining complete audit trail of support interactions and providing customer with documented resolution process.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_support_ticket_id
foreignFields.description: Parent support ticket this message belongs to. {@link ecommerce_mall_support_tickets.id}.

foreignFields.name: created_by_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Customer who created this message (if message from customer). Null if message from support agent. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}.

foreignFields.name: created_by_admin_id
foreignFields.description: Admin who created this message (if message from support agent). Null if message from customer. {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}.

plainFields.name: message_text
plainFields.description: Content of the support message. Supports formatted text and basic markdown for emphasis and links.

plainFields.name: is_internal
plainFields.description: Flag indicating if this is an internal note visible only to support team, not to customer. Allows private team discussion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the message was created. Messages are immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, message is hidden but retained for audit trail and historical reference.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_knowledge_base_articles
models.description:
Self-service support articles providing detailed help content and guides.

Comprehensive knowledge base for customer self-service support. Articles cover topics like how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, policy explanations, product specifications, and common solutions. Customers can search and browse articles to resolve issues independently without contacting support.

Articles are organized by support category and tagged for searchability. Each article tracks view counts, helpfulness ratings, and search engine optimization metadata (SEO). Articles support draft and published states, allowing content creators to prepare articles before making them public.

Articles include detailed content with formatted text support for better readability and understanding. Publishing metadata enables content freshness tracking and automatic archival of outdated articles.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_support_category_id
foreignFields.description: Support category this knowledge base article belongs to. Enables browsing articles by topic. {@link ecommerce_mall_support_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description: Article title as displayed to customers. Should be clear and descriptive of article content. Examples: 'How to Track Your Order', 'Understanding Our Return Policy'.

plainFields.name: slug
plainFields.description: URL-friendly slug for article identification. Used in knowledge base URLs. Lowercase with hyphens. Example: 'how-to-track-order'.

plainFields.name: content
plainFields.description: Full article content with detailed explanation, steps, images, or examples. Supports formatted text (bold, italic, lists, links) for rich content presentation.

plainFields.name: summary
plainFields.description: Brief summary of article content for search results and preview displays. Maximum 200 characters.

plainFields.name: meta_description
plainFields.description: SEO meta description for search engine result snippets. Helps with search visibility and click-through rates.

plainFields.name: meta_keywords
plainFields.description: Comma-separated keywords for article search engine optimization. Improves article discoverability in searches.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Publication status: draft (not visible), published (visible to customers), archived (hidden but preserved). Enables content versioning and scheduling.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this article has been viewed by customers. Used for popularity metrics and content effectiveness analysis.

plainFields.name: helpful_count
plainFields.description: Number of times customers marked this article as helpful. Used to identify high-quality, effective content.

plainFields.name: unhelpful_count
plainFields.description: Number of times customers marked this article as not helpful. Indicates articles needing review or updating.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the knowledge base article was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the knowledge base article was last updated with new content or corrections.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when article was published and made visible to customers. Null if article is still in draft status.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, article is archived and removed from search results but retained for historical reference.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_faq_items
models.description:
Frequently asked questions providing quick answers to common customer inquiries.

Curated collection of frequently asked questions and their concise answers. FAQs provide quick reference for common issues, policies, and procedures. Customers can quickly search FAQs for answers before submitting support tickets.

Each FAQ item consists of a question and answer pair. FAQs are organized by support category for easy navigation. Items track view counts and helpful votes to identify most valuable content and guide content curation.

FAQs are simpler and more concise than full knowledge base articles, providing quick answers rather than detailed guides. Published FAQs are visible to customers; draft FAQs are used for preparation. Soft deletion enables content management while preserving historical records.
