foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_support_category_id
foreignFields.description: Support category this FAQ item belongs to. Enables browsing FAQs by topic area. {@link ecommerce_mall_support_categories.id}.

plainFields.name: question
plainFields.description: The frequently asked question. Should be phrased as customer would ask it. Examples: 'How long does shipping take?', 'What is your return policy?'.

plainFields.name: answer
plainFields.description: Concise answer to the question. Should be brief but complete, providing the information needed without excessive detail. Supports formatted text.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Publication status: draft (not visible), published (visible to customers), archived (hidden). Enables content management and versioning.

plainFields.name: display_order
plainFields.description: Sort order for displaying FAQ items. Lower numbers appear first in category FAQ lists.

plainFields.name: view_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this FAQ has been viewed by customers. Used for popularity and engagement metrics.

plainFields.name: helpful_count
plainFields.description: Number of times customers marked this FAQ as helpful. Indicates high-quality, useful FAQs.

plainFields.name: unhelpful_count
plainFields.description: Number of times customers marked this FAQ as not helpful. Indicates FAQs needing review or updating.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the FAQ item was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the FAQ item was last updated with new content or corrections.

plainFields.name: published_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when FAQ was published and made visible to customers. Null if FAQ is still in draft status.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Soft delete timestamp. When set, FAQ is archived and removed from listings but retained for historical reference.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_event_log
models.description:
Raw event tracking for user behavior and system activities. Captures granular, time-series events including page views, purchases, reviews, errors, and platform actions. This table serves as the authoritative source for all business activity analytics and user behavior patterns.

Each event record contains a timestamp, event type classification, actor information (customer or seller), and flexible event data stored as JSON to accommodate diverse event types without schema modifications. This append-only, immutable log enables comprehensive historical analysis and reconstructing user journeys.

The event_log is optimized for high-volume ingestion and time-range queries, with indexes supporting efficient filtering by timestamp, event type, and actor. Events are retained for 12 months with older events archived to cold storage for compliance and historical analysis.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to customer who triggered the event. Nullable for guest events or seller-initiated events. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to seller who triggered the event. Nullable for customer or guest events. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to product involved in the event. Nullable for non-product events. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_order_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to order involved in the event. Nullable for non-order events. {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Classification of the event. Examples: product_view, product_add_to_cart, checkout_initiated, order_placed, payment_processed, shipment_created, delivery_confirmed, review_submitted, seller_product_created, seller_order_fulfilled. Used for event filtering and categorization.

plainFields.name: event_category
plainFields.description: Higher-level grouping of event types. Values: customer_activity, seller_activity, product_activity, order_activity, payment_activity, shipping_activity, review_activity, system_activity, error_activity. Enables broad event filtering and dashboard segmentation.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor triggering the event. Values: guest, customer, seller, admin, system. Determines which IDs are populated and how event is attributed.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: IP address from which event originated. Used for geographic analysis, fraud detection, and user behavior tracking. Stored for compliance with up to 12 months retention.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: HTTP User-Agent header identifying browser, device, and operating system. Enables device-type segmentation and OS analysis for platform optimization.

plainFields.name: event_data
plainFields.description: Flexible JSON object containing event-specific data. Structure varies by event_type. Examples: {product_id, quantity, price} for purchase events; {review_rating, review_length} for review events. Enables extensibility without schema changes.

plainFields.name: session_id
plainFields.description: Session identifier for grouping related events from same user session. Enables session-based analytics and user journey reconstruction.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when event occurred, in UTC. Critical for time-series analysis and temporal queries. Events are immutable after creation.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_daily_metrics
models.description:
Daily aggregated performance metrics calculated from event_log. Provides pre-calculated key metrics by date for efficient dashboard and report generation. Each record represents a single day's aggregated data across the entire platform.

Metrics captured include total orders, revenue, active users (customers and sellers), page views, search queries, product views, cart additions, conversion rates, payment success rate, and order cancellation rate. These daily snapshots enable trend analysis and performance monitoring without requiring real-time aggregation of millions of events.

Daily metrics are recalculated each day at off-peak hours (2 AM UTC) and immutable once calculated. Historical daily metrics enable week-over-week and year-over-year comparisons for business intelligence.

plainFields.name: metric_date
plainFields.description: Date for which metrics are calculated (UTC midnight). One record per day. Format: YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00 UTC. Used as identifier for daily metrics.

plainFields.name: total_orders
plainFields.description: Total number of orders placed on this date. Includes all order types (single seller, multi-seller). Orders only counted if payment was successfully authorized.

plainFields.name: total_revenue
plainFields.description: Total gross revenue from all orders placed on this date. Includes product prices, shipping, taxes. Does not deduct refunds (captured separately). In primary currency (USD equivalent).

plainFields.name: total_refunds
plainFields.description: Total refund amount issued on this date (when refund was processed, not when requested). Enables net revenue calculation.

plainFields.name: active_customers
plainFields.description: Number of unique customers who generated at least one event on this date. Includes page views, clicks, purchases, reviews, etc.

plainFields.name: active_sellers
plainFields.description: Number of unique sellers who generated at least one event on this date. Includes product uploads, order fulfillments, etc.

plainFields.name: new_customer_registrations
plainFields.description: Number of new customer accounts created on this date. Tracks customer acquisition rate.

plainFields.name: new_seller_registrations
plainFields.description: Number of new seller accounts created on this date. Tracks seller acquisition rate.

plainFields.name: page_views
plainFields.description: Total number of page views across the platform on this date. Includes product pages, category pages, seller stores, etc.

plainFields.name: product_views
plainFields.description: Number of product detail page views on this date. Indicates product discovery activity.

plainFields.name: search_queries
plainFields.description: Number of search queries executed on this date. Tracks search volume and product discovery patterns.

plainFields.name: cart_additions
plainFields.description: Number of items added to shopping carts on this date. Indicates purchase intent.

plainFields.name: checkout_initiations
plainFields.description: Number of checkouts started on this date. Excludes completions (see total_orders). Enables cart abandonment analysis.

plainFields.name: payment_success_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of payment attempts that succeeded on this date. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Calculated as (successful_payments / total_payment_attempts) * 100.

plainFields.name: order_cancellation_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of orders that were cancelled on this date. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Calculated as (cancelled_orders / total_orders) * 100.

plainFields.name: reviews_submitted
plainFields.description: Number of product reviews submitted on this date. Tracks customer engagement and feedback volume.

plainFields.name: average_order_value
plainFields.description: Average revenue per order on this date. Calculated as total_revenue / total_orders. Indicates customer spending patterns.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when daily metrics were calculated. Typically 2 AM UTC on the day following metric_date.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_monthly_metrics
models.description:
Monthly aggregated performance metrics calculated from daily_metrics or event_log. Provides high-level monthly summaries for executive reporting and year-over-year comparisons. Each record represents all aggregated activity for a calendar month.

Monthly metrics include total orders, revenue, customer acquisition, seller acquisition, average metrics, and trend indicators. These monthly rollups enable executive dashboards to track business growth, seasonal patterns, and performance trends without needing to aggregate raw events.

Monthly metrics are immutable once calculated (first day of following month). Historical monthly data supports strategic planning and business intelligence for growth analysis.

plainFields.name: year
plainFields.description: Calendar year for which metrics are calculated. Examples: 2024, 2025. Used with month to identify metric period.

plainFields.name: month
plainFields.description: Calendar month (1-12) for which metrics are calculated. Combined with year to identify month. Range: 1 (January) to 12 (December).

plainFields.name: total_orders
plainFields.description: Total number of orders placed during the month. Sum of daily_metrics.total_orders for the month.

plainFields.name: total_revenue
plainFields.description: Total gross revenue from all orders in the month. Sum of daily_metrics.total_revenue for the month. In USD equivalent.

plainFields.name: total_refunds
plainFields.description: Total refunds issued in the month. Sum of daily_metrics.total_refunds for the month.

plainFields.name: net_revenue
plainFields.description: Net revenue after refunds. Calculated as total_revenue - total_refunds. True economic value in the month.

plainFields.name: unique_customers
plainFields.description: Total number of unique customers who had at least one event during the month. Distinct count from daily active_customers.

plainFields.name: unique_sellers
plainFields.description: Total number of unique sellers who had at least one event during the month. Distinct count from daily active_sellers.

plainFields.name: new_customer_registrations
plainFields.description: Number of new customer accounts created during the month. Sum of daily new_customer_registrations.

plainFields.name: new_seller_registrations
plainFields.description: Number of new seller accounts created during the month. Sum of daily new_seller_registrations.

plainFields.name: total_page_views
plainFields.description: Total page views across platform during the month. Sum of daily page_views.

plainFields.name: total_product_views
plainFields.description: Total product detail page views during the month. Sum of daily product_views.

plainFields.name: total_search_queries
plainFields.description: Total search queries executed during the month. Sum of daily search_queries.

plainFields.name: total_reviews_submitted
plainFields.description: Total product reviews submitted during the month. Sum of daily reviews_submitted.

plainFields.name: average_order_value
plainFields.description: Average order value for the month. Calculated as total_revenue / total_orders. Indicates customer spending level.

plainFields.name: average_payment_success_rate
plainFields.description: Average daily payment success rate for the month. Calculated as average of daily_metrics.payment_success_rate for the month.

plainFields.name: average_order_cancellation_rate
plainFields.description: Average daily order cancellation rate for the month. Calculated as average of daily_metrics.order_cancellation_rate for the month.

plainFields.name: customer_retention_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of customers from previous month who made a purchase in this month. Indicates customer retention. Range: 0.0 to 100.0.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when monthly metrics were calculated. Typically first day of following month.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_product_metrics
models.description:
Product-level performance metrics tracking individual product sales, popularity, and customer satisfaction. Aggregated daily from event_log capturing product-specific activity. Each record represents performance metrics for a specific product on a specific date.

Metrics include units sold, revenue, page views, click-through rate, conversion rate, customer rating, and review count. These product metrics enable sellers to understand which products perform well, which underperform, and identify optimization opportunities.

Daily product metrics are calculated each day at off-peak hours and support seller dashboards, product search ranking optimization, and inventory management decision-making.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_product_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the product being tracked. {@link ecommerce_mall_products.id}

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller who owns the product. Enables seller-level product analytics. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: metric_date
plainFields.description: Date for which product metrics are calculated (UTC midnight). One record per product per day. Format: YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00 UTC.

plainFields.name: units_sold
plainFields.description: Number of units of this product sold on this date. Aggregated from order items.

plainFields.name: revenue
plainFields.description: Total revenue from this product on this date. Calculated as sum of (unit_price × quantity) for all orders containing this product.

plainFields.name: page_views
plainFields.description: Number of times the product detail page was viewed on this date. Indicates product visibility and interest.

plainFields.name: add_to_cart_count
plainFields.description: Number of times this product was added to shopping carts on this date. Indicates purchase intent.

plainFields.name: conversion_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of product page views that resulted in purchase on this date. Calculated as (units_sold / page_views) * 100. Range: 0.0 to 100.0+.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Current average rating for this product (as of this date). Captured daily to track rating changes over time. Range: 1.0 to 5.0.

plainFields.name: review_count
plainFields.description: Total number of reviews/ratings for this product (as of this date). Tracked daily to monitor review accumulation.

plainFields.name: new_reviews
plainFields.description: Number of new reviews submitted for this product on this date. Indicates feedback velocity.

plainFields.name: refund_count
plainFields.description: Number of orders containing this product that were refunded on this date. Indicates product quality or satisfaction issues.

plainFields.name: stock_level
plainFields.description: Current available inventory level for this product (as of end of this date). Tracked daily to monitor stock depletion.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when product metrics were calculated. Typically 2 AM UTC on the day following metric_date.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_metrics
models.description:
Seller-level performance metrics aggregated daily from order and review data. Tracks individual seller sales performance, customer satisfaction, fulfillment quality, and operational efficiency. Each record represents aggregated metrics for a specific seller on a specific date.

Metrics include total orders, revenue, average order value, shipping speed, refund rate, customer satisfaction ratings, and fulfillment performance. Sellers use these metrics to monitor their store performance and understand customer satisfaction.

Daily seller metrics support seller dashboards, performance badges, search ranking optimization, and business intelligence. Metrics are recalculated daily at off-peak hours.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_seller_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the seller being tracked. {@link ecommerce_mall_sellers.id}

plainFields.name: metric_date
plainFields.description: Date for which seller metrics are calculated (UTC midnight). One record per seller per day. Format: YYYY-MM-DD 00:00:00 UTC.

plainFields.name: total_orders
plainFields.description: Number of orders placed from this seller on this date. Includes completed, pending, and cancelled orders.

plainFields.name: total_revenue
plainFields.description: Total gross revenue from orders placed with this seller on this date. Does not deduct refunds.

plainFields.name: average_order_value
plainFields.description: Average order value for orders from this seller on this date. Calculated as total_revenue / total_orders.

plainFields.name: customer_count
plainFields.description: Number of unique customers who purchased from this seller on this date.

plainFields.name: new_customers
plainFields.description: Number of first-time customers of this seller on this date. Indicates new customer acquisition.

plainFields.name: repeat_customers
plainFields.description: Number of returning customers who purchased again from this seller on this date. Indicates customer loyalty.

plainFields.name: fulfillment_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of orders from this seller that were fulfilled (shipped) on time during this date range. Range: 0.0 to 100.0.

plainFields.name: average_shipping_speed_hours
plainFields.description: Average hours from order confirmation to shipment dispatch for this seller on this date. Lower is better. Indicates fulfillment speed.

plainFields.name: refund_count
plainFields.description: Number of refunds issued for orders from this seller on this date.

plainFields.name: refund_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of this seller's orders that were refunded. Calculated as (refund_count / total_orders) * 100. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. High rates indicate quality issues.

plainFields.name: average_rating
plainFields.description: Current average rating for this seller (as of this date). Calculated from all customer reviews. Range: 1.0 to 5.0.

plainFields.name: new_reviews
plainFields.description: Number of new reviews/ratings for this seller on this date.

plainFields.name: customer_satisfaction_score
plainFields.description: Overall customer satisfaction metric for this seller on this date. Calculated from average rating and review sentiment. Range: 0.0 to 100.0.

plainFields.name: cancellation_count
plainFields.description: Number of orders from this seller that were cancelled on this date.

plainFields.name: cancellation_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of this seller's orders that were cancelled on this date. Calculated as (cancellation_count / total_orders) * 100. Range: 0.0 to 100.0.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when seller metrics were calculated. Typically 2 AM UTC on the day following metric_date.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_segments
models.description:
Customer cohort analysis and segmentation data for targeted marketing and business intelligence. Captures customer groupings by acquisition date (cohorts), spending patterns, and engagement levels. Enables cohort-based retention analysis and customer lifetime value (CLV) calculations.

Segmentation includes customer cohorts (grouped by registration month), customer value segments (high/medium/low value based on lifetime spend), engagement segments (active/moderate/inactive based on purchase frequency), and acquisition channel segments (organic/paid/referral).

Customer segments are recalculated monthly to reflect changing customer status and value. Segments enable targeted retention campaigns and help identify at-risk customers for proactive engagement.

foreignFields.name: ecommerce_mall_customer_id
foreignFields.description: Reference to the customer being segmented. {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}

plainFields.name: cohort_month
plainFields.description: Registration month (1-12) of the customer's cohort. Customers registered in same month are grouped into same cohort.

plainFields.name: cohort_year
plainFields.description: Registration year of the customer's cohort. Combined with cohort_month to identify the cohort period.

plainFields.name: value_segment
plainFields.description: Customer value classification based on lifetime spend and purchase frequency. Values: high_value (>90th percentile spending), medium_value (40-90th percentile), low_value (<40th percentile). Enables targeted retention strategies.

plainFields.name: engagement_segment
plainFields.description: Customer engagement level based on purchase frequency and recent activity. Values: active (purchased in last 30 days), moderate (purchased in last 90 days), inactive (no purchases in 90+ days). Identifies at-risk customers.

plainFields.name: acquisition_channel
plainFields.description: How customer was acquired to the platform. Values: organic (direct/search), paid (advertising), referral (referred by existing customer), affiliate (partner program). Enables marketing ROI analysis.

plainFields.name: lifetime_spend
plainFields.description: Total lifetime spending by this customer across all orders. Enables CLV analysis and value segmentation.

plainFields.name: lifetime_orders
plainFields.description: Total number of orders placed by this customer. Indicates purchase frequency and engagement.

plainFields.name: repeat_purchase_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of customers in this cohort who made repeat purchases (2+ orders). Calculated as (repeat_customers / cohort_size) * 100. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Indicates cohort retention.

plainFields.name: average_order_value
plainFields.description: Average order value for this customer. Calculated as lifetime_spend / lifetime_orders. Indicates customer spending capacity.

plainFields.name: last_purchase_date
plainFields.description: Date of this customer's most recent order. Used to identify at-risk customers (no recent purchases).

plainFields.name: days_since_last_purchase
plainFields.description: Number of days since this customer's last purchase. Calculated daily. Used to determine engagement_segment.

plainFields.name: churn_risk
plainFields.description: Assessment of likelihood customer will churn (stop purchasing). Values: high (inactive 90+ days), medium (inactive 30-90 days), low (active purchase within 30 days). Identifies customers for retention campaigns.

plainFields.name: segment_updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when customer segment was last calculated or updated. Typically monthly recalculation.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when customer segment record was created (when customer segment analysis started).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_performance_metrics
models.description:
System and platform performance tracking metrics capturing infrastructure health, API performance, and operational status. Metrics include server response times, database performance, error rates, payment processor performance, and external service integrations. Enables operational monitoring and SLA (Service Level Agreement) compliance tracking.

Performance metrics are collected and aggregated hourly from multiple monitoring sources (application logs, infrastructure monitoring, third-party integrations). These metrics feed into operational dashboards and trigger alerts when performance falls below targets.

Metrics support incident response (understanding performance during issues), performance optimization (identifying bottlenecks), and capacity planning (understanding growth trends). Performance data is retained for 1 year.

plainFields.name: metric_hour
plainFields.description: Hour for which performance metrics are collected (UTC rounded to hour boundary). Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:00:00 UTC. One record per hour.

plainFields.name: api_response_time_p95
plainFields.description: 95th percentile API response time in milliseconds for this hour. Indicates response time for most (95%) of API requests. Target: <500ms.

plainFields.name: api_response_time_p99
plainFields.description: 99th percentile API response time in milliseconds for this hour. Indicates slowest acceptable response times. Target: <2000ms.

plainFields.name: search_response_time_p95
plainFields.description: 95th percentile search API response time in milliseconds. Target: <1000ms.

plainFields.name: database_query_time_p95
plainFields.description: 95th percentile database query execution time in milliseconds. Target: <100ms.

plainFields.name: error_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of API requests that resulted in error (5xx response codes) during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Target: <0.1%.

plainFields.name: payment_processor_availability
plainFields.description: Percentage of time payment processor API was available during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Target: >99.9%.

plainFields.name: shipping_provider_availability
plainFields.description: Percentage of time shipping provider APIs were available during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Target: >99%.

plainFields.name: server_cpu_usage_percent
plainFields.description: Average CPU usage percentage across all application servers during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Alert threshold: >80%.

plainFields.name: server_memory_usage_percent
plainFields.description: Average memory usage percentage across all application servers during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Alert threshold: >85%.

plainFields.name: database_cpu_usage_percent
plainFields.description: Database server CPU usage during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Alert threshold: >80%.

plainFields.name: database_connection_count
plainFields.description: Average number of active database connections during this hour. Alert threshold: >80% of pool size.

plainFields.name: requests_per_second
plainFields.description: Average number of API requests per second handled during this hour. Indicates traffic volume.

plainFields.name: concurrent_users
plainFields.description: Peak number of concurrent users on the platform during this hour.

plainFields.name: uptime_percent
plainFields.description: Percentage of time platform was available during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Target: >99.9%.

plainFields.name: cache_hit_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of cache requests that hit cache (vs going to database) during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Higher is better (less DB load).

plainFields.name: payment_success_rate
plainFields.description: Percentage of payment attempts that succeeded during this hour. Range: 0.0 to 100.0. Target: >99.5%.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when performance metrics were collected/calculated.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_audit_log
models.description:
Complete system-wide audit trail of all significant platform events.

This table captures every meaningful action across the platform including user activities, system changes, administrative operations, and automated processes. It serves as the authoritative record for compliance, investigation, and troubleshooting.

The audit log is immutable (append-only) and designed to support GDPR compliance, financial auditing, security investigations, and regulatory requirements. All records include who performed the action, what was affected, when it occurred, and relevant context.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor who performed the action. Valid values: admin, system, automation, customer, seller. Identifies the source/origin of the action for filtering and investigation.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: ID of the actor who performed the action. References admin, customer, or seller account. Nullable for system-initiated events with no specific actor.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Categorizes the specific action performed. Examples: create, update, delete, access, approve, suspend, payment_processed. Used for filtering events by action category in compliance reports.

plainFields.name: resource_type
plainFields.description: Identifies the type of resource affected by the action. Examples: order, product, customer, seller, payment, inventory. Enables finding all events related to specific resource types.

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: ID of the specific resource affected by the action. Links audit event to the affected entity for investigation and correlation. Nullable for system-wide events not tied to specific resource.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed natural-language description of what happened, why it happened, and the outcome. Provides human-readable context for audit investigators reviewing compliance reports.

plainFields.name: changes
plainFields.description: JSON object containing before/after values for modification events. Captures what changed during update operations. Format: {"field_name": {"old": value, "new": value}}. Null for non-modification events.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description: JSON object with additional contextual information. May include: IP address, HTTP method, request path, user agent, session ID, geographic location, error codes. Used for security investigations and trend analysis.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when the audit event was recorded. Defines event ordering and enables time-range queries for compliance reports and investigations. No update_at field (immutable append-only log).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_admin_actions
models.description:
Audit trail of all administrative actions and changes made by platform administrators.

Tracks every action taken by admins including user management (suspension, approval), configuration changes, commission adjustments, dispute resolutions, and operational decisions. This is the authoritative record for admin accountability and oversight.

Each record documents the admin who took the action, what was changed, old and new values, the business reason for the action, and approval chain for sensitive operations. Designed for admin accountability, compliance review, and operational investigation.

foreignFields.name: admin_id
foreignFields.description: References the admin who performed the action. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id} to identify accountability. Enables tracking all actions by specific admin.

foreignFields.name: approved_by_id
foreignFields.description: References the admin who approved this action if dual-approval was required. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}. Null for actions not requiring secondary approval. Documents approval chain.

plainFields.name: action_type
plainFields.description: Specific admin action performed. Examples: create_user, approve_seller, suspend_account, adjust_commission, update_category, resolve_dispute, delete_product, update_settings. Enables filtering admin actions by type.

plainFields.name: resource_type
plainFields.description: Type of resource affected by admin action. Examples: customer, seller, product, category, setting, configuration, commission_rate. Identifies what was being managed.

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: ID of the specific resource that was affected by the admin action. Links to the resource being managed (customer ID, product ID, seller ID, etc.) for investigation and correlation.

plainFields.name: old_value
plainFields.description: JSON representation of the resource's state before the admin action. Null if action was creation (no previous state). Enables before/after comparison for change analysis.

plainFields.name: new_value
plainFields.description: JSON representation of the resource's state after the admin action. Contains the actual values that were set/changed. May be null if action was deletion.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Business reason for the admin action. Examples: 'Seller violated quality standards', 'Customer fraud detected', 'Platform maintenance', 'Commission adjustment per agreement'. Required for all admin actions for accountability.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when the admin action was executed. Defines action ordering and enables investigation of admin decisions in chronological order. No update_at (immutable record).

models.name: ecommerce_mall_data_access_log
models.description:
Comprehensive log of all access to sensitive customer and business data for GDPR and privacy compliance.

Tracks every query, export, or access to personally identifiable information (PII) and sensitive business data. This is critical for GDPR Subject Access Requests, privacy audits, and detecting unauthorized access patterns.

Records identify who accessed what data, when, from where, and for what purpose. Enables investigation of data breaches, compliance with data retention policies, and validation that access controls are working properly.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of entity accessing data. Valid values: admin, system, customer, seller. Identifies the class of user accessing sensitive data for access control verification.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: ID of the specific user/admin/system accessing the data. Links to customer, seller, or admin account. Enables tracking all data accessed by specific user for GDPR subject access requests.

plainFields.name: data_category
plainFields.description: Category of sensitive data accessed. Examples: customer_pii, customer_email, customer_address, payment_data, order_history, seller_bank_info, admin_config. Enables filtering access by data sensitivity level.

plainFields.name: resource_type
plainFields.description: Type of resource containing the data. Examples: customer, seller, order, payment, product, support_ticket. Identifies entity type being accessed.

plainFields.name: resource_id
plainFields.description: ID of the specific resource whose data was accessed. Links to customer, seller, order, etc. Enables finding all data access for specific subject in compliance investigations.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: Source IP address from which data was accessed. Identifies location of access for geographic anomaly detection and investigating unauthorized access from unexpected locations.

plainFields.name: purpose
plainFields.description: Stated purpose for accessing data. Examples: customer_support, fraud_investigation, billing_verification, analytics, compliance_audit. Validates that access has legitimate business reason.

plainFields.name: row_count
plainFields.description: Number of data rows/records accessed in this access event. Helps identify suspicious large-scale data exports or queries. High counts may indicate data breach attempt.

plainFields.name: duration_ms
plainFields.description: Duration of the data access operation in milliseconds. Helps identify slow queries that might indicate performance issues or suspicious activity. Typical query 50-500ms.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when the data access occurred. Enables time-range queries for investigating data access patterns around specific incidents. Immutable record.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_inventory_adjustments_audit
models.description:
Immutable audit trail of all inventory quantity adjustments for accountability and discrepancy investigation.

Records every change to inventory levels including system-generated adjustments from orders, manual corrections by sellers, damage/loss adjustments, and admin interventions. Enables complete reconstruction of inventory history and investigation of discrepancies.

Each adjustment includes quantity before/after, reason for change, who made the adjustment, and approval chain for large adjustments. Supports inventory audits, detects anomalies, and proves accountability for inventory accuracy.

foreignFields.name: product_sku_id
foreignFields.description: References the specific product SKU whose inventory was adjusted. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_product_skus.id}. Enables finding all adjustments for specific product variant.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: References the order related to this inventory adjustment (if applicable). Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}. Null for non-order-related adjustments (damage, loss, correction). For returns/fulfillments.

foreignFields.name: approver_id
foreignFields.description: References the admin who approved this adjustment (for large adjustments requiring approval). Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_admins.id}. Null for small adjustments not requiring approval. Documents approval chain.

plainFields.name: adjustment_type
plainFields.description: Type of inventory adjustment performed. Valid values: increase (restocking), decrease (sold/lost), correction (physical count correction), return (customer return received), loss (damage/theft). Categorizes adjustment purpose.

plainFields.name: quantity_before
plainFields.description: Inventory quantity before the adjustment. Enables verification of before-state. Zero or positive integer representing available units.

plainFields.name: quantity_adjusted
plainFields.description: Quantity changed by the adjustment. Can be positive (increase) or negative (decrease). Allows recalculating: quantity_after = quantity_before + quantity_adjusted.

plainFields.name: quantity_after
plainFields.description: Inventory quantity after the adjustment. Enables verification of after-state. Must be non-negative. System enforces: quantity_after >= 0.

plainFields.name: reason
plainFields.description: Business reason for the inventory adjustment. Examples: 'Restock received from supplier', 'Physical count discrepancy (actual 15 vs system 12)', 'Customer return received', '3 units damaged in transit'. Required for all adjustments.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of actor making the adjustment. Valid values: seller, admin, system. Identifies who is responsible for this inventory change.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: ID of the actor (seller or admin) who requested/performed the adjustment. Links to seller or admin account for accountability.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when the inventory adjustment was recorded. Enables chronological reconstruction of inventory history. Immutable audit record.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_payment_audit_log
models.description:
Comprehensive PCI DSS-compliant audit trail of all payment transactions and processing events.

Records every payment interaction including authorization requests, capture, refunds, and failures. This is the authoritative record for payment compliance, chargeback disputes, and financial auditing. Critical for PCI DSS Level 1 compliance.

Documents payment method type, processor response codes, transaction success/failure, associated customer and order, and source IP. Does NOT store sensitive payment data (card numbers, CVV) - only references tokens from payment processors. Enables investigation of payment issues, fraud detection, and regulatory compliance.

foreignFields.name: order_id
foreignFields.description: References the order associated with this payment. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_orders.id}. Enables finding payment history for specific order and correlating payment with fulfillment.

foreignFields.name: customer_id
foreignFields.description: References the customer who made the payment. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_customers.id}. Enables finding all payments by customer and detecting fraud patterns.

plainFields.name: payment_method_type
plainFields.description: Type of payment method used. Valid values: credit_card, debit_card, digital_wallet, bank_transfer, other. Identifies payment method for analysis and compliance reporting.

plainFields.name: transaction_id
plainFields.description: External transaction ID from payment processor (Stripe charge ID, PayPal transaction ID, etc.). Unique identifier for payment processor's transaction for reconciliation and dispute resolution.

plainFields.name: amount
plainFields.description: Transaction amount in specified currency. Positive number representing funds transferred. Used for financial reconciliation and sales reporting.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description: Currency code for the transaction (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, etc.). Three-letter ISO 4217 code. Used for multi-currency financial reporting.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description: Payment transaction status. Valid values: authorized, captured, failed, refunded, disputed, pending. Indicates outcome of payment processing. Critical for order reconciliation.

plainFields.name: processor_name
plainFields.description: Name of the payment processor handling the transaction. Examples: Stripe, PayPal, Square, Authorize.net. Identifies which service processed the payment.

plainFields.name: response_code
plainFields.description: Response code returned by payment processor. Examples: '100' (success), '201' (unsuccessful), '202' (error). Provides detailed reason for transaction outcome.

plainFields.name: error_message
plainFields.description: Error message from processor if transaction failed. Examples: 'Insufficient funds', 'Card expired', 'CVV mismatch'. Null for successful transactions. Helps diagnose payment issues.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: Source IP address from which payment was initiated. Used for fraud detection (comparing against historical customer IPs). Identifies geographic location of payment.

plainFields.name: merchant_reference
plainFields.description: Internal merchant reference/order number for this transaction. Links payment processor's records to our system. Used for reconciliation between systems.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when payment was processed. Enables time-based queries for financial reporting and chargeback investigations. Immutable audit record per PCI DSS requirements.

models.name: ecommerce_mall_security_events
models.description:
Comprehensive security incident and anomaly log for breach detection, investigation, and forensics.

Tracks all security-related events including suspicious login attempts, rate limit violations, fraud detections, policy violations, and account lockouts. Critical for security monitoring, incident response, and post-breach forensics.

Each event is classified by type and severity, includes the affected account and source IP, documents remediation taken, and links to related support investigations. Enables identifying security patterns, detecting coordinated attacks, and proving security posture to regulators and stakeholders.

foreignFields.name: ticket_id
foreignFields.description: References related support ticket if security event required investigation. Links to {@link ecommerce_mall_support_tickets.id}. Null if event was automatically remediated without ticket. Links security events to support system.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description: Classification of security event. Valid values: suspicious_login, rate_limit_exceeded, fraud_detected, breach_attempt, policy_violation, account_locked, unusual_activity. Categorizes security incident type.

plainFields.name: severity
plainFields.description: Severity level of security event. Valid values: critical, high, medium, low, info. Determines response priority and escalation. Critical events require immediate action.

plainFields.name: actor_type
plainFields.description: Type of account involved in security event. Valid values: customer, seller, admin, anonymous. Null for events not tied to specific actor type. Identifies who was affected.

plainFields.name: actor_id
plainFields.description: ID of the account involved in security event. References customer, seller, or admin account. Null for anonymous events (external breach attempts, etc.). Identifies affected user.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description: Source IP address of security event. Used for geographic anomaly detection and identifying attack sources. Enables blocking malicious IPs and trend analysis.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description: Browser/client user agent string from security event. Identifies device type and software making the suspicious request. Null for non-web events. Helps identify automated attacks.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Detailed description of the security incident. Examples: 'Failed login attempt from unusual country (China) for US-based customer', '50 requests per second from IP 192.168.1.1', 'Credit card fraud pattern detected'. Provides context for investigation.

plainFields.name: remediation_taken
plainFields.description: Description of remediation actions taken in response to security event. Examples: 'Account temporarily locked and password reset required', 'IP address blocked', 'Transaction reversed'. Null if no automatic remediation. Documents response actions.

plainFields.name: investigation_notes
plainFields.description: JSON object containing detailed investigation notes and findings. May include: analyst name, analysis date, root cause, impact assessment, recommendations. Null until investigation completes. Captures investigation results.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: UTC timestamp when security event was recorded. Defines event sequence for forensics. Enables time-based queries for breach investigations and timeline reconstruction. Immutable record.
